/**
 * Mock Auth API â€” implements the AuthApi contract against the mock database.
 *
 * Security model (mirrors what a hardened real backend must do):
 * - Passwords hashed with PBKDF2-SHA256 (see security.ts); never stored/logged
 *   in plaintext and never included in any API response.
 * - Brute-force lockout: 5 consecutive failed logins locks the account for
 *   15 minutes (429 RATE_LIMITED).
 * - Generic login errors ("Invalid email or password") so attackers cannot
 *   enumerate registered emails.
 * - Sessions: 256-bit random tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes; access
 *   tokens expire after 24h; refresh tokens after 30 days (or 12h when the
 *   user did NOT check "remember me") and are ROTATED on every refresh.
 * - "Remember me" scopes the session to localStorage vs sessionStorage.
 */
import type {
  AuthResponse,
  GoogleLoginRequest,
  LoginRequest,
  PasswordResetRequest,
  PasswordResetResponse,
  RefreshTokenResponse,
  RegisterRequest,
  ResetPasswordRequest,
  User,
  VerifyResetCodeRequest,
  VerifyResetCodeResponse,
} from '../types';
import type { AuthApi } from '../services/auth';
import { mockDb, generateId, nowIso } from './mockDatabase';
import type { MockSession, StoredUser } from './mockDatabase';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';
import { assertValidGoogleClaims, decodeGoogleIdToken } from './googleIdToken';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';
import { sessionStore, type TokenPersistMode } from '../session';
import {
  generateSecureToken,
  hashPassword,
  sha256Hex,
  validatePasswordStrength,
  verifyPassword,
} from './security';

/** Access tokens are deliberately short-lived. */
const ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours
/** Refresh token lifetime for remembered sessions. */
const REFRESH_TTL_REMEMBERED_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 30 days
/** Refresh token lifetime when the user did not check "remember me". */
const REFRESH_TTL_SESSION_MS = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 12 hours
/** Brute-force lockout thresholds. */
const MAX_FAILED_LOGINS = 5;
const LOCKOUT_DURATION_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000; // 15 minutes
/** Password reset OTP configuration. */
const OTP_LENGTH = 6;
const OTP_TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000; // 15 minutes
const MAX_OTP_ATTEMPTS = 3;

function toPublicUser(stored: StoredUser): User {
  const { passwordHash: _p, failedLoginCount: _f, lockedUntil: _l, ...publicUser } = stored;
  return publicUser;
}

/**
 * Issue a fresh session: random tokens, hashed into the DB, stored client-side.
 * Returns the raw pair so callers can hand it to the client exactly like a
 * real login/refresh response would.
 */
async function issueSession(
  userId: string,
  remember: boolean,
): Promise<{ accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }> {
  const accessToken = generateSecureToken();
  const refreshToken = generateSecureToken();
  const now = Date.now();
  const session: MockSession = {
    id: generateId(),
    userId,
    accessTokenHash: await sha256Hex(accessToken),
    refreshTokenHash: await sha256Hex(refreshToken),
    accessExpiresAt: now + ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS,
    refreshExpiresAt: now + (remember ? REFRESH_TTL_REMEMBERED_MS : REFRESH_TTL_SESSION_MS),
    createdAt: nowIso(),
    lastUsedAt: nowIso(),
  };
  mockDb.insert('sessions', session);
  const persist: TokenPersistMode = remember ? 'local' : 'session';
  sessionStore.setTokens({ accessToken, refreshToken }, persist);
  return { accessToken, refreshToken };
}

function assertNotLocked(user: StoredUser): void {
  if (user.lockedUntil && user.lockedUntil > Date.now()) {
    const minutes = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((user.lockedUntil - Date.now()) / 60_000));
    throw new ApiError({
      message: `Too many failed attempts. This account is locked for ${minutes} more minute(s).`,
      status: 429,
      code: 'RATE_LIMITED',
    });
  }
}

async function registerFailedLogin(user: StoredUser): Promise<void> {
  const count = (user.failedLoginCount ?? 0) + 1;
  const lockedUntil = count >= MAX_FAILED_LOGINS ? Date.now() + LOCKOUT_DURATION_MS : null;
  mockDb.update('users', user.id, { failedLoginCount: count, lockedUntil } as never);
}

function clearFailedLogins(userId: string): void {
  mockDb.update('users', userId, { failedLoginCount: 0, lockedUntil: null } as never);
}

export class MockAuthApi implements AuthApi {
  async register(data: RegisterRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/register');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const fullName = data.fullName?.trim() ?? '';
      const email = data.email?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      const password = data.password ?? '';

      const fieldErrors: Record<string, string> = {};
      if (!fullName) fieldErrors.fullName = 'Full name is required';
      else if (fullName.length < 2 || fullName.length > 80) {
        fieldErrors.fullName = 'Full name must be between 2 and 80 characters';
      }
      if (!email) fieldErrors.email = 'Email is required';
      else if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email) || email.length > 254) {
        fieldErrors.email = 'Enter a valid email';
      }
      if (!password) fieldErrors.password = 'Password is required';
      else {
        const policy = validatePasswordStrength(password);
        if (!policy.ok) fieldErrors.password = policy.error ?? 'Password does not meet the requirements';
      }
      if (!data.accountType) fieldErrors.accountType = 'Account type is required';

      if (Object.keys(fieldErrors).length > 0) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors,
        });
      }

      const existing = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === email);
      if (existing.length > 0) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'An account with this email already exists.',
          status: 409,
          code: 'EMAIL_TAKEN',
          fieldErrors: { email: 'Email is already registered' },
        });
      }

      const timestamp = nowIso();
      const user = mockDb.insert('users', {
        id: generateId(),
        email,
        fullName,
        accountType: data.accountType,
        avatarUrl: null,
        status: 'active',
        createdAt: timestamp,
        updatedAt: timestamp,
        passwordHash: await hashPassword(password),
        failedLoginCount: 0,
        lockedUntil: null,
      } as never);

      // A fresh registration is always a remembered session.
      const tokens = await issueSession(user.id, true);
      return { user: toPublicUser(user as StoredUser), tokens };
    })());
  }

  async login(data: LoginRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/login');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const email = data.email?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      const password = data.password ?? '';

      if (!email || !password) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Email and password are required.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { email: 'Email is required', password: 'Password is required' },
        });
      }

      const user = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === email)[0];
      // One generic error for every failure path â€” never reveal whether the
      // email exists (prevents account enumeration).
      const invalidCredentials = new ApiError({
        message: 'Invalid email or password.',
        status: 401,
        code: 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS',
      });

      if (!user) throw invalidCredentials;
      assertNotLocked(user);

      const passwordOk = await verifyPassword(password, user.passwordHash);
      if (!passwordOk) {
        await registerFailedLogin(user);
        throw invalidCredentials;
      }

      if (user.status !== 'active') {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'This account has been suspended. Contact support for help.',
          status: 403,
          code: 'FORBIDDEN',
        });
      }

      clearFailedLogins(user.id);
      // rememberMe=false scopes tokens to sessionStorage (dies with the tab).
      const tokens = await issueSession(user.id, data.rememberMe ?? true);
      return { user: toPublicUser(user), tokens };
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Google sign-in/sign-up â€” POST /auth/google.
   *
   * Receives the REAL Google ID token (JWT) produced by Google Identity
   * Services. The real backend verifies its signature against Google's
   * public keys; the mock decodes the payload and validates the standard
   * claims (expiry, audience, issuer, verified email) exactly as
   * google-auth-library would after verification â€” see googleIdToken.ts.
   *
   * - Email already registered â†’ the EXISTING user is authenticated. No
   *   duplicate account is ever created (account linking). The only field
   *   ever backfilled is a missing avatar, adopted from the Google picture.
   * - Email unknown â†’ a new user row following the existing user schema is
   *   created with `authProvider: "google"`. Because Google accounts have no
   *   password, an UNGUESSABLE random one is hashed into `passwordHash` so
   *   the schema invariant (always a pbkdf2$ hash) holds while email/password
   *   login can never succeed for the account.
   *
   * The response is the same AuthResponse shape used by login/register, plus
   * `isNewUser` so the UI can run signup-style redirects.
   */
  async googleLogin(data: GoogleLoginRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/google');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const credential = data?.credential;
      if (typeof credential !== 'string' || !credential.trim()) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'A Google credential is required.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
        });
      }

      // Decode + validate the ID token claims. Real backend: signature
      // verification against Google's JWKS happens here too.
      const claims = decodeGoogleIdToken(credential.trim());
      assertValidGoogleClaims(claims);

      const email = typeof claims.email === 'string' ? claims.email.trim().toLowerCase() : '';
      if (!email || !/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email) || email.length > 254) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'The Google account has no usable email address.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { credential: 'The Google account has no usable email address.' },
        });
      }
      const fullName =
        (typeof claims.name === 'string' && claims.name.trim().slice(0, 80)) ||
        [claims.given_name, claims.family_name]
          .filter((part): part is string => typeof part === 'string' && part.trim().length > 0)
          .map((part) => part.trim())
          .join(' ') ||
        email.split('@')[0];
      const picture = typeof claims.picture === 'string' ? claims.picture.trim() : '';

      // Existing account â†’ link & log in (never create a duplicate).
      const existing = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === email)[0];
      if (existing) {
        if (existing.status !== 'active') {
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'This account has been suspended. Contact support for help.',
            status: 403,
            code: 'FORBIDDEN',
          });
        }
        clearFailedLogins(existing.id);
        let user = existing;
        if (picture && !user.avatarUrl) {
          // Light-touch linking: adopt the Google picture only when the
          // account has no avatar yet. Nothing else is overwritten.
          user = (mockDb.update('users', user.id, { avatarUrl: picture }) as StoredUser) ?? user;
        }
        const tokens = await issueSession(user.id, data.rememberMe ?? true);
        return { user: toPublicUser(user), tokens, isNewUser: false };
      }

      // New Google signup â†’ create the user following the existing schema.
      const accountType = data.accountType === 'buyer' ? 'buyer' : 'seller';
      const timestamp = nowIso();
      const user = mockDb.insert('users', {
        id: generateId(),
        email,
        fullName,
        accountType,
        avatarUrl: picture || null,
        status: 'active',
        createdAt: timestamp,
        updatedAt: timestamp,
        passwordHash: await hashPassword(generateSecureToken()),
        failedLoginCount: 0,
        lockedUntil: null,
        authProvider: 'google',
      } as never);

      // A fresh Google registration is always a remembered session.
      const tokens = await issueSession(user.id, true);
      return { user: toPublicUser(user as StoredUser), tokens, isNewUser: true };
    })());
  }

  async logout(): Promise<void> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/logout');
    // Revoke the entire server-side session (access + refresh) for this token.
    const token = sessionStore.getAccessToken();
    if (token) {
      const tokenHash = await sha256Hex(token);
      mockDb
        .query('sessions', (s) => s.accessTokenHash === tokenHash)
        .forEach((s) => mockDb.remove('sessions', s.id));
    }
    sessionStore.clear();
    return withMockLatency(undefined);
  }

  async getCurrentUser(): Promise<User> {
    logApi('GET', '/auth/me');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const token = sessionStore.getAccessToken();
      if (!token) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Not authenticated.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      const tokenHash = await sha256Hex(token);
      const session = mockDb.query('sessions', (s) => s.accessTokenHash === tokenHash)[0];
      if (!session) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Session expired.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      if (session.accessExpiresAt <= Date.now()) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Session expired.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      const user = mockDb.findById('users', session.userId);
      if (!user) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'User not found.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      return toPublicUser(user as StoredUser);
    })());
  }

  async refreshToken(refreshToken: string): Promise<RefreshTokenResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/refresh');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      if (!refreshToken) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Refresh token required.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      // SECURITY: actually validate the presented refresh token, then ROTATE
      // it â€” the old pair is revoked and cannot be replayed.
      const refreshHash = await sha256Hex(refreshToken);
      const session = mockDb.query('sessions', (s) => s.refreshTokenHash === refreshHash)[0];
      if (!session || session.refreshExpiresAt <= Date.now()) {
        sessionStore.clear();
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Invalid or expired refresh token.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }
      const user = mockDb.findById('users', session.userId);
      if (!user || user.status !== 'active') {
        mockDb.remove('sessions', session.id);
        sessionStore.clear();
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Session cannot be refreshed.', status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
      }

      mockDb.remove('sessions', session.id);
      const persist: TokenPersistMode = sessionStore.currentPersistMode();
      const accessToken = generateSecureToken();
      const newRefreshToken = generateSecureToken();
      const now = Date.now();
      mockDb.insert('sessions', {
        id: generateId(),
        userId: session.userId,
        accessTokenHash: await sha256Hex(accessToken),
        refreshTokenHash: await sha256Hex(newRefreshToken),
        accessExpiresAt: now + ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS,
        // Rotation never extends beyond the original refresh window.
        refreshExpiresAt: Math.min(session.refreshExpiresAt, now + REFRESH_TTL_REMEMBERED_MS),
        createdAt: session.createdAt,
        lastUsedAt: nowIso(),
      } as never);
      const tokens = { accessToken, refreshToken: newRefreshToken };
      sessionStore.setTokens(tokens, persist);
      return tokens;
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Request password reset â€” generates a 6-digit OTP and simulates emailing it.
   *
   * SECURITY:
   * - Generic response whether email exists or not (prevents enumeration).
   * - Old OTPs for the same email are revoked when a new one is requested.
   * - OTP expires after 15 minutes.
   * - Rate limiting: 3 failed verification attempts lock the OTP.
   * - Development mode returns the OTP in devOtp for testing.
   */
  async requestPasswordReset(data: PasswordResetRequest): Promise<PasswordResetResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/forgot-password');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const email = data.email?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';

      if (!email || !/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email)) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please enter a valid email address.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { email: 'Please enter a valid email address.' },
        });
      }

      const user = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === email)[0];

      // Generic success response whether the email exists or not â€” prevents
      // attackers from enumerating registered accounts.
      const genericResponse: PasswordResetResponse = {
        message: 'If an account exists with this email, a verification code has been sent.',
      };

      if (!user) {
        // Email not found â€” still return success to prevent enumeration.
        return genericResponse;
      }

      // Generate a 6-digit OTP.
      const code = Array.from({ length: OTP_LENGTH }, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 10)).join('');
      const expiresAt = Date.now() + OTP_TTL_MS;

      // Revoke any existing OTPs for this email.
      mockDb.query('passwordResetOTPs', (otp) => otp.email === email).forEach((otp) => mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id));

      // Store the new OTP.
      mockDb.insert('passwordResetOTPs', {
        id: generateId(),
        email,
        code,
        expiresAt,
        createdAt: nowIso(),
        failedAttempts: 0,
      } as never);

      // Development-only: log OTP to console and return in response for testing.
      if (import.meta.env.DEV) {
        console.log('\nðŸ“§ [MOCK EMAIL] Password Reset OTP');
        console.log(`To: ${email}`);
        console.log(`Subject: Your verification code`);
        console.log(`\nYour verification code is: ${code}`);
        console.log(`This code expires in 15 minutes.\n`);
        return { ...genericResponse, devOtp: code };
      }

      return genericResponse;
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Verify password reset OTP.
   *
   * SECURITY:
   * - Rate limiting: 3 failed attempts invalidate the OTP.
   * - Expired OTPs are automatically rejected.
   * - Verified OTPs remain valid for the final resetPassword step.
   */
  async verifyResetCode(data: VerifyResetCodeRequest): Promise<VerifyResetCodeResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/verify-reset-code');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const email = data.email?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      const code = data.code?.trim() ?? '';

      if (!email || !code) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Email and verification code are required.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Verification code is required.' },
        });
      }

      // Clean up expired OTPs first.
      const now = Date.now();
      mockDb.query('passwordResetOTPs', (otp) => otp.expiresAt <= now).forEach((otp) => mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id));

      const otp = mockDb.query('passwordResetOTPs', (o) => o.email === email)[0];

      if (!otp) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Invalid or expired verification code.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Invalid or expired verification code.' },
        });
      }

      if (otp.expiresAt <= now) {
        mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id);
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Verification code has expired. Please request a new one.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Verification code has expired.' },
        });
      }

      if (otp.failedAttempts >= MAX_OTP_ATTEMPTS) {
        mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id);
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Too many failed attempts. Please request a new verification code.',
          status: 429,
          code: 'RATE_LIMITED',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Too many failed attempts.' },
        });
      }

      if (otp.code !== code) {
        // Increment failed attempts.
        mockDb.update('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id, { failedAttempts: otp.failedAttempts + 1 } as never);
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Incorrect verification code.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Incorrect verification code.' },
        });
      }

      // OTP verified successfully â€” keep it for the final reset step.
      return { message: 'Verification code confirmed.', verified: true };
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Complete password reset with verified OTP and new password.
   *
   * SECURITY:
   * - Requires a valid, non-expired OTP that has been verified.
   * - Password strength validation enforced.
   * - OTP is consumed (deleted) after successful password reset.
   * - All existing sessions for the user are revoked (security best practice).
   */
  async resetPassword(data: ResetPasswordRequest): Promise<{ message: string }> {
    logApi('POST', '/auth/reset-password');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const email = data.email?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      const code = data.code?.trim() ?? '';
      const newPassword = data.newPassword ?? '';

      if (!email || !code || !newPassword) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Email, verification code, and new password are required.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
        });
      }

      // Validate password strength.
      const policy = validatePasswordStrength(newPassword);
      if (!policy.ok) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: policy.error ?? 'Password does not meet the requirements.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'WEAK_PASSWORD',
          fieldErrors: { newPassword: policy.error ?? 'Password does not meet the requirements.' },
        });
      }

      // Clean up expired OTPs.
      const now = Date.now();
      mockDb.query('passwordResetOTPs', (otp) => otp.expiresAt <= now).forEach((otp) => mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id));

      const otp = mockDb.query('passwordResetOTPs', (o) => o.email === email && o.code === code)[0];

      if (!otp || otp.expiresAt <= now) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Invalid or expired verification code.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { code: 'Invalid or expired verification code.' },
        });
      }

      const user = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === email)[0];
      if (!user) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'User not found.',
          status: 404,
          code: 'NOT_FOUND',
        });
      }

      // Update password.
      const passwordHash = await hashPassword(newPassword);
      mockDb.update('users', user.id, { passwordHash, failedLoginCount: 0, lockedUntil: null } as never);

      // Revoke the OTP (single-use).
      mockDb.remove('passwordResetOTPs', otp.id);

      // SECURITY: revoke all existing sessions for this user so stolen sessions
      // can't continue after a password change.
      mockDb.query('sessions', (s) => s.userId === user.id).forEach((s) => mockDb.remove('sessions', s.id));

      return { message: 'Password reset successfully. You can now log in with your new password.' };
    })());
  }
}

/**
 * Google ID token (JWT) handling for the mock backend.
 *
 * The REAL backend verifies the token's signature against Google's public
 * keys (JWKS) plus the aud/iss/exp claims. The mock cannot verify signatures
 * (it has no Google keys), so it performs the SAME claim validation after
 * decoding the payload â€” when Django lands, the missing piece inside
 * POST /auth/google is exactly one signature-verification step.
 */
import { apiConfig } from '../config';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import type { GoogleIdTokenPayload } from '../types';

/** Small clock-skew allowance, like real token libraries apply. */
const CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS = 60;

function base64UrlToBytes(segment: string): Uint8Array {
  const base64 = segment.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
  const padded = base64 + '='.repeat((4 - (base64.length % 4)) % 4);
  const binary = atob(padded);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}

/** Decode the payload of a Google ID token (JWT) without verifying it. */
export function decodeGoogleIdToken(credential: string): GoogleIdTokenPayload {
  if (credential.length > 5000) {
    throw new ApiError({ message: 'Invalid Google credential.', status: 422, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' });
  }
  const parts = credential.split('.');
  if (parts.length !== 3 || parts[1].length === 0) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'Invalid Google credential. Expected a Google ID token.',
      status: 422,
      code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
    });
  }
  try {
    const payload = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(base64UrlToBytes(parts[1]))) as GoogleIdTokenPayload;
    if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload)) {
      throw new Error('Token payload is not an object.');
    }
    return payload;
  } catch {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'Invalid Google credential. The token payload could not be decoded.',
      status: 422,
      code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Validate the standard ID-token claims the way the real backend will after
 * signature verification: expiry, audience, issuer, verified email.
 */
export function assertValidGoogleClaims(payload: GoogleIdTokenPayload): void {
  const nowSeconds = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);

  if (typeof payload.exp !== 'number' || payload.exp < nowSeconds - CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'Your Google session expired. Please try signing in again.',
      status: 401,
      code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
    });
  }

  if (apiConfig.googleClientId) {
    const audiences = Array.isArray(payload.aud) ? payload.aud : [payload.aud];
    if (!audiences.includes(apiConfig.googleClientId)) {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'This Google sign-in is not valid for this application (audience mismatch).',
        status: 401,
        code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
      });
    }
  }

  const issuer = typeof payload.iss === 'string' ? payload.iss.replace(/\/+$/, '') : '';
  if (issuer !== 'https://accounts.google.com' && issuer !== 'accounts.google.com') {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'This Google sign-in did not come from Google (untrusted issuer).',
      status: 401,
      code: 'UNAUTHORIZED',
    });
  }

  if (payload.email_verified === false) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'Your Google account email is not verified. Verify it at accounts.google.com and try again.',
      status: 403,
      code: 'FORBIDDEN',
    });
  }
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\mock\mockDatabase.ts =====

/**
 * Centralized mock database.
 *
 * Single source of truth for every piece of mock-persisted data. Persists to
 * localStorage so data survives page refreshes. Components NEVER touch
 * localStorage â€” they go through the API services, and the services go through
 * this module.
 */
import type { Order, Product, SellerProfile, User } from '../types';
import { seedDatabase } from './seed';

// v4: orders now carry line `items` (productId/productName/quantity/
// unitPrice/lineTotal/sellerId) â€” old v3 rows had no items, so seller
// analytics could not attribute revenue; v3 data is reseeded.
export const MOCK_DB_KEY = 'universe.mockdb.v4';

/**
 * A mock "server-side" session record.
 *
 * SECURITY: raw tokens are never persisted â€” only their SHA-256 hashes are.
 * Access tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens are longer-lived and are
 * rotated (invalidated) on every refresh, so a stolen refresh token can't be
 * replayed forever.
 */
export interface MockSession {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  accessTokenHash: string;
  refreshTokenHash: string;
  accessExpiresAt: number;
  refreshExpiresAt: number;
  createdAt: string;
  lastUsedAt: string;
}

/**
 * Password reset OTP record.
 *
 * SECURITY: OTPs are time-limited (15 minutes) and single-use. After
 * verification or expiry, they are deleted. Rate limiting prevents brute-force
 * attacks (3 failed attempts within 15 minutes locks the email temporarily).
 */
export interface PasswordResetOTP {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  code: string;
  expiresAt: number;
  createdAt: string;
  /** Failed verification attempts counter for rate limiting. */
  failedAttempts: number;
}

/** Internal user row â€” includes fields the API responses strip out. */
export interface StoredUser extends User {
  /** PBKDF2 hash (pbkdf2$<iter>$<salt>$<hash>) â€” never returned to clients. */
  passwordHash: string;
  /** Brute-force protection: consecutive failed login attempts. */
  failedLoginCount?: number;
  /** Timestamp (ms) until which login attempts are locked out. */
  lockedUntil?: number | null;
  phone?: string | null;
  /**
   * How the account was created/authenticates. Google-created rows get
   * 'google'; password rows keep the default (undefined === 'password').
   */
  authProvider?: 'password' | 'google';
}

export interface MockDatabaseShape {
  users: StoredUser[];
  sessions: MockSession[];
  passwordResetOTPs: PasswordResetOTP[];
  sellerProfiles: SellerProfile[];
  products: Product[];
  orders: Order[];
  /** Auto-increment counters used to generate stable numeric-looking ids. */
  counters: Record<string, number>;
}

/**
 * The record-array collections â€” every collection except `counters`, which is
 * bookkeeping metadata rather than a list. The list helpers below never touch
 * `counters`, and excluding it here keeps their generic types sound (a
 * `Record<string, number>` cannot be `.find()`-ed or `[number]`-indexed).
 */
type ArrayCollections = Omit<MockDatabaseShape, 'counters'>;
type CollectionName = keyof ArrayCollections;

function clone<T>(value: T): T {
  if (typeof structuredClone === 'function') return structuredClone(value);
  return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T;
}

/**
 * Load the DB (seeding from seed.ts on first run / if the stored schema is
 * missing/older than the current version).
 */
function readDb(): MockDatabaseShape {
  try {
    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(MOCK_DB_KEY);
    if (raw) {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as MockDatabaseShape;
      // Validate the schema shape so an older/partial database is reseeded
      // instead of being trusted (e.g. passwords must be PBKDF2 hashes, and
      // sessions must store token hashes â€” never plaintext values).
      const usersOk =
        parsed &&
        Array.isArray(parsed.users) &&
        parsed.users.length > 0 &&
        typeof parsed.users[0].passwordHash === 'string' &&
        parsed.users[0].passwordHash.startsWith('pbkdf2$');
      const sessionsOk =
        parsed &&
        Array.isArray(parsed.sessions) &&
        (parsed.sessions.length === 0 || 'accessTokenHash' in parsed.sessions[0]);
      if (usersOk && sessionsOk && parsed.counters) {
        return parsed;
      }
    }
  } catch {
    /* corrupted storage â€” reseed */
  }
  const fresh = seedDatabase();
  writeDb(fresh);
  return fresh;
}

function writeDb(db: MockDatabaseShape): void {
  window.localStorage.setItem(MOCK_DB_KEY, JSON.stringify(db));
}

export function nowIso(): string {
  return new Date().toISOString();
}

export function generateId(): string {
  if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && typeof crypto.randomUUID === 'function') {
    return crypto.randomUUID();
  }
  return `mock-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
}

function nextId(db: MockDatabaseShape, collection: CollectionName): number {
  const next = (db.counters[collection] ?? 0) + 1;
  db.counters[collection] = next;
  return next;
}

export const mockDb = {
  /** Return a deep copy of a full collection. */
  getCollection<K extends CollectionName>(name: K): ArrayCollections[K] {
    return clone(readDb()[name]);
  },

  /** Replace a full collection. */
  setCollection<K extends CollectionName>(name: K, items: ArrayCollections[K]): void {
    const db = readDb();
    db[name] = clone(items) as MockDatabaseShape[K];
    writeDb(db);
  },

  findById<K extends CollectionName>(name: K, id: string): ArrayCollections[K][number] | null {
    const item = readDb()[name].find((entry) => (entry as { id: string }).id === id);
    return item ? clone(item) : null;
  },

  query<K extends CollectionName>(name: K, predicate: (item: ArrayCollections[K][number]) => boolean): ArrayCollections[K][number][] {
    return readDb()[name].filter(predicate).map((item) => clone(item)) as ArrayCollections[K][number][];
  },

  /** Insert a record; assigns id + createdAt when missing. */
  insert<K extends CollectionName>(name: K, item: ArrayCollections[K][number]): ArrayCollections[K][number] {
    const db = readDb();
    const entry = clone(item) as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (!entry.id) entry.id = generateId();
    if (!entry.createdAt) entry.createdAt = nowIso();
    if (!entry.updatedAt) entry.updatedAt = entry.createdAt;
    // The union of record arrays is not directly comparable to a mutable
    // Record list (interfaces carry no index signatures), hence the bridge.
    (db[name] as unknown as Array<Record<string, unknown>>).push(entry);
    writeDb(db);
    return clone(entry) as unknown as ArrayCollections[K][number];
  },

  /** Update a record by id; returns the updated record or null. */
  update<K extends CollectionName>(name: K, id: string, patch: Partial<ArrayCollections[K][number]>): ArrayCollections[K][number] | null {
    const db = readDb();
    // Same bridge as insert(): operate on the row as a plain record.
    const list = db[name] as unknown as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    const index = list.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === id);
    if (index === -1) return null;
    list[index] = { ...list[index], ...clone(patch as Record<string, unknown>), updatedAt: nowIso() };
    writeDb(db);
    return clone(list[index]) as unknown as ArrayCollections[K][number];
  },

  /** Remove a record by id; returns true if removed. */
  remove(name: CollectionName, id: string): boolean {
    const db = readDb();
    const list = db[name] as Array<{ id: string }>;
    const index = list.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === id);
    if (index === -1) return false;
    list.splice(index, 1);
    writeDb(db);
    return true;
  },

  /** Insert-scope id generator, useful for reference-style numeric ids. */
  getNextId(collection: CollectionName): number {
    const db = readDb();
    return nextId(db, collection);
  },

  /** Wipe everything and reseed â€” useful for "Reset demo data" style flows. */
  reset(): void {
    const fresh = seedDatabase();
    writeDb(fresh);
  },
};

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\mock\mockLatency.ts =====

/**
 * Simulated network latency for the mock API.
 *
 * Every mock endpoint awaits withMockLatency() before resolving (success or
 * failure), so loading/error/empty states behave like a real network. Disable
 * it during development with VITE_MOCK_LATENCY=off.
 */
import { apiConfig } from '../config';

export function mockDelayMs(): number {
  const { enabled, min, max } = apiConfig.mockLatency;
  if (!enabled) return 0;
  return Math.round(min + Math.random() * (max - min));
}

/** Wait for a simulated network round-trip (300â€“800ms by default). */
export async function withMockLatency<T>(value: T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const ms = mockDelayMs();
  // Endpoints call this with an already-started promise, so a failing request
  // rejects while the latency timer is still ticking. Attaching a no-op handler
  // NOW marks that rejection as handled (the caller still receives it through
  // the returned promise) and keeps expected 4xx responses from being reported
  // as "unhandled rejection" console noise.
  if (value instanceof Promise) value.catch(() => {});
  if (ms > 0) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => window.setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  }
  return value;
}

/**
 * Mock Orders API â€” implements the OrdersApi contract against the mock DB.
 *
 * SIMULATION SCOPE: the mock may simulate successful order creation (it is a
 * development stand-in for the real backend). The REAL adapter never does.
 *
 * Behavior:
 * - createOrder validates the payload the same way the contract requires the
 *   real backend to (non-empty items, quantities >= 1, delivery address
 *   fields) and, when a paymentReference is supplied, requires a payment the
 *   mock payments API has verified in this browser.
 * - Orders are scoped to the signed-in buyer; other users never see them.
 * - getOrders/getOrder paginate over the buyer's own orders (newest first).
 */
import type { CreateOrderRequest, Order, OrderItem, OrderQueryParams, PaginatedResponse } from '../types';
import type { OrdersApi } from '../services/orders';
import { mockDb, generateId, nowIso } from './mockDatabase';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';
import { requireSession } from './sessionGuard';
import { verifiedPaymentAmount } from './payments.mock';

/** Internal row shape â€” adds ownership fields the API responses strip out. */
interface StoredOrder extends Order {
  buyerId: string;
}

function failField(fieldErrors: Record<string, string>): never {
  throw new ApiError({
    message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
    status: 422,
    code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
    fieldErrors,
  });
}

export class MockOrdersApi implements OrdersApi {
  async getOrders(params: OrderQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Order>> {
    logApi('GET', '/orders');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const mine = mockDb
        .query('orders', (o) => (o as StoredOrder).buyerId === user.id)
        .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt));
      const page = Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1);
      const pageSize = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, params.pageSize ?? 20));
      const start = (page - 1) * pageSize;
      return {
        items: mine.slice(start, start + pageSize),
        total: mine.length,
        page,
        pageSize,
      };
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Seller-side order list: orders containing at least one product the
   * signed-in seller owns, newest first. Sales Analytics reads from this, so
   * every number it shows is derived from real order rows â€” this mock only
   * replays what the mock DB holds, exactly like the real backend will.
   */
  async getSellerOrders(params: OrderQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Order>> {
    logApi('GET', '/seller/orders');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      if (user.accountType !== 'seller') {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Only seller accounts can view seller orders.',
          status: 403,
          code: 'FORBIDDEN',
        });
      }
      const since = params.since ? new Date(params.since).getTime() : null;
      const until = params.until ? new Date(params.until).getTime() : null;
      const mine = mockDb
        .query('orders', (o) => {
          const order = o as StoredOrder;
          // A seller sees an order only when one of THEIR products is on it.
          if (!Array.isArray(order.items) || !order.items.some((item) => item.sellerId === user.id)) {
            return false;
          }
          const created = new Date(order.createdAt).getTime();
          if (Number.isNaN(created)) return false;
          if (since != null && created < since) return false;
          if (until != null && created > until) return false;
          return true;
        })
        .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt));
      const page = Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1);
      const pageSize = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, params.pageSize ?? 20));
      const start = (page - 1) * pageSize;
      return {
        items: mine.slice(start, start + pageSize),
        total: mine.length,
        page,
        pageSize,
      };
    })());
  }

  async getOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> {
    logApi('GET', `/orders/${id}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const order = mockDb.findById('orders', id) as StoredOrder | null;
      // Hide the existence of other buyers' orders (404, not 403).
      if (!order || order.buyerId !== user.id) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Order not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      return order;
    })());
  }

  async createOrder(data: CreateOrderRequest): Promise<Order> {
    logApi('POST', '/orders');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();

      const errors: Record<string, string> = {};
      if (!Array.isArray(data.items) || data.items.length === 0) {
        errors.items = 'Add at least one item before placing the order';
      }
      const delivery = data.deliveryAddress;
      if (!delivery || typeof delivery !== 'object') {
        errors.deliveryAddress = 'Delivery information is required';
      } else {
        if (!delivery.fullName?.trim()) errors['deliveryAddress.fullName'] = 'Full name is required';
        if (!delivery.phone?.trim()) errors['deliveryAddress.phone'] = 'Phone number is required';
        if (!delivery.addressLine1?.trim()) errors['deliveryAddress.addressLine1'] = 'Address is required';
        if (!delivery.city?.trim()) errors['deliveryAddress.city'] = 'City is required';
      }
      if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) failField(errors);

      // Build the REAL line items from the catalog: the CATALOG owns the
      // price (mirrors the real backend recomputing totals) and each line
      // carries its sellerId so seller analytics can attribute revenue.
      const items: OrderItem[] = [];
      for (const item of data.items) {
        const product = mockDb.findById('products', item.productId);
        if (!product || product.status !== 'active') {
          // Same anti-enumeration stance as the products API.
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'One of the items is no longer available.',
            status: 404,
            code: 'NOT_FOUND',
          });
        }
        if (!Number.isInteger(item.quantity) || item.quantity < 1 || item.quantity > 99) {
          failField({ items: 'Quantities must be between 1 and 99' });
        }
        const unitPrice = product.salePrice ?? product.price;
        items.push({
          productId: product.id,
          productName: product.name,
          quantity: item.quantity,
          unitPrice,
          lineTotal: unitPrice != null ? unitPrice * item.quantity : null,
          sellerId: product.sellerId ?? null,
        });
      }

      // Payment must be verified BEFORE order creation when a reference is
      // part of the flow (contract rule; see docs/API_CONTRACT.md).
      let amount: number | null = null;
      if (data.paymentReference) {
        const verified = verifiedPaymentAmount(data.paymentReference);
        if (verified === null) {
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'This payment has not been verified. Complete the payment first.',
            status: 402,
            code: 'CONFLICT',
          });
        }
        amount = verified;
      } else {
        amount = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + (item.lineTotal ?? 0), 0);
      }

      const timestamp = nowIso();
      const order: StoredOrder = {
        id: generateId(),
        reference: `UNI-${Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase()}`,
        buyerId: user.id,
        buyerName: user.fullName,
        buyerInitials: user.fullName
          .split(/\s+/)
          .map((part) => part.charAt(0).toUpperCase())
          .slice(0, 2)
          .join(''),
        amount,
        // Fresh orders always start as "processing" â€” the backend owns any
        // later transitions.
        status: 'processing',
        createdAt: timestamp,
        items,
      };
      return mockDb.insert('orders', order as never);
    })());
  }
}

/**
 * Mock Payments API â€” simulates the Paystack-via-backend flow for
 * development. The mock ALWAYS "succeeds" after its simulated latency: this
 * is deliberate development behavior and is the ONLY place a payment success
 * may be fabricated. The real adapter (real/payments.api.ts) reports success
 * exclusively from the backend's verification response.
 *
 * The verified amounts are tracked in-memory so the mock orders API can
 * enforce the same "pay first, then order" rule the contract demands.
 */
import type {
  PaymentInitializationRequest,
  PaymentInitializationResponse,
  PaymentVerificationResponse,
} from '../types';
import type { PaymentsApi } from '../services/payments';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';

/** reference -> verified amount (major units). Simulated Paystack ledger. */
const verifiedPayments = new Map<string, number>();

/**
 * The amount the mock "Paystack" verified for a reference, or null when the
 * reference was never initialized/verified. Used by MockOrdersApi to refuse
 * orders that did not go through payment.
 */
export function verifiedPaymentAmount(reference: string): number | null {
  return verifiedPayments.get(reference) ?? null;
}

export class MockPaymentsApi implements PaymentsApi {
  async initializePayment(
    data: PaymentInitializationRequest,
  ): Promise<PaymentInitializationResponse> {
    logApi('POST', '/payments/initialize');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const amount = Number(data.amount);
      if (!Number.isFinite(amount) || amount <= 0) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { amount: 'Amount must be a positive number' },
        });
      }
      if (!data.email || !/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(data.email)) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { email: 'Enter a valid email' },
        });
      }
      const reference = `PS-MOCK-${Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase()}`;
      // Simulated ledger entry â€” the buyer "pays" instantly in mock mode.
      verifiedPayments.set(reference, Math.round(amount * 100) / 100);
      return {
        // A stand-in checkout URL: in real mode the backend returns the
        // actual Paystack authorization_url.
        authorizationUrl: `https://checkout.paystack.com/${reference.toLowerCase()}`,
        reference,
        status: 'success',
      };
    })());
  }

  async verifyPayment(reference: string): Promise<PaymentVerificationResponse> {
    logApi('GET', `/payments/verify/${reference}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const amount = verifiedPayments.get(reference);
      if (amount === undefined) {
        // Unknown reference â€” reported as failed, the way an unverified
        // transaction must read to the order flow.
        return { reference, status: 'failed', amount: null, paidAt: null, orderId: null };
      }
      return {
        reference,
        status: 'success',
        amount,
        currency: 'NGN',
        transactionId: reference,
        paidAt: new Date().toISOString(),
        orderId: null,
      };
    })());
  }
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\mock\products.mock.ts =====

/**
 * Mock Products API â€” implements the ProductsApi contract against the mock DB.
 *
 * SECURITY MODEL (ownership & privacy):
 * - createProduct requires a session â€” products are always owned by the
 *   authenticated seller, never "unknown".
 * - updateProduct / deleteProduct require BOTH a session AND ownership of the
 *   product. A non-owned id returns 404 (not 403) so attackers cannot use the
 *   error to enumerate other sellers' product ids.
 * - Draft products are private: they are hidden from listings and cannot be
 *   fetched by anyone except their owner.
 * - The public catalog (no sellerId) only ever returns active products that
 *   the seller has FEATURED â€” at most MARKETPLACE_LISTING_LIMIT (2) per seller.
 * - Every write is validated & sanitized server-side (length caps, numeric
 *   bounds, enum whitelists, URL scheme checks).
 */
import type {
  CreateProductRequest,
  Product,
  ProductQueryParams,
  PaginatedResponse,
  ProductVariant,
  UpdateProductRequest,
} from '../types';
import { MARKETPLACE_LISTING_LIMIT, WORKSHOP_PRODUCT_LIMIT } from '../types';
import type { ProductsApi } from '../services/products';
import { mockDb, generateId, nowIso } from './mockDatabase';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';
import { requireSession, getSessionUserSafe } from './sessionGuard';

/** Whitelist of allowed product categories (mirrors the UI select). */
export const PRODUCT_CATEGORIES = [
  'Fashion',
  'Electronics',
  'Gadgets',
  'Books',
  'Others',
] as const;

/** Caps for the seller-entered variant option groups. */
const MAX_VARIANTS = 10;
const MAX_VARIANT_VALUES = 20;
const MAX_VARIANT_TEXT = 40;

/**
 * Default listing order â€” newest first.
 *
 * The mock stores rows in insertion order, so without this a seller's brand-new
 * product is appended behind every older row and silently falls off the first
 * page of any paginated listing (the marketplace's catalog is paginated). Order
 * is the backend's job (docs/API_CONTRACT.md), so the mock mirrors the "Newest
 * first" default the workshop UI offers, keeping fresh listings discoverable.
 */
function byNewestFirst(a: Product, b: Product): number {
  return (Date.parse(b.createdAt) || 0) - (Date.parse(a.createdAt) || 0);
}

function withSellerProfile(product: Product): Product {
  const profile = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (entry) => entry.userId === product.sellerId)[0];
  return {
    ...product,
    seller: profile?.storeName || product.seller,
    sellerLogo: profile?.logoUrl ?? null,
    sellerPhone: profile?.phone ?? null,
  };
}

/** Count the seller's OTHER active products currently featured in the marketplace. */
function countOtherFeatured(
  sellerId: string,
  excludeProductId: string | null,
): number {
  return mockDb.query('products', (p) => (
    p.sellerId === sellerId
    && p.id !== excludeProductId
    && p.status === 'active'
    && p.featuredInMarketplace === true
  )).length;
}

/**
 * Enforce the listing cap when a product would become featured. Throws a 422
 * with a clear message when the seller already has the maximum number of
 * active products featured in the marketplace.
 */
function enforceListingLimit(
  sellerId: string,
  productId: string | null,
  willBeFeatured: boolean,
): void {
  if (!willBeFeatured) return;
  const otherFeatured = countOtherFeatured(sellerId, productId);
  if (otherFeatured >= MARKETPLACE_LISTING_LIMIT) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: `You can list at most ${MARKETPLACE_LISTING_LIMIT} products in the public marketplace. Remove one first, then try again.`,
      status: 422,
      code: 'MARKETPLACE_LIMIT_REACHED',
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Enforce the workshop product cap (WORKSHOP_PRODUCT_LIMIT, active + drafts
 * combined) when creating a new product. Throws a 422 with a clear message
 * when the seller has already filled every slot.
 */
function enforceWorkshopLimit(sellerId: string): void {
  const ownedCount = mockDb.query('products', (p) => p.sellerId === sellerId).length;
  if (ownedCount >= WORKSHOP_PRODUCT_LIMIT) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: `Your workshop is full â€” you can store up to ${WORKSHOP_PRODUCT_LIMIT} products. Remove one first, then try again.`,
      status: 422,
      code: 'WORKSHOP_LIMIT_REACHED',
    });
  }
}

function failField(fieldErrors: Record<string, string>): never {
  throw new ApiError({
    message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
    status: 422,
    code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
    fieldErrors,
  });
}

function checkText(value: string | null | undefined, field: string, max: number, errors: Record<string, string>): void {
  if (value !== undefined && value !== null && value.trim().length > max) {
    errors[field] = `Must be ${max} characters or fewer`;
  }
}

function checkPrice(value: number | null | undefined, field: string, errors: Record<string, string>): void {
  if (value === undefined || value === null) return;
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    errors[field] = 'Price must be a positive number';
  } else if (value > 10_000_000) {
    errors[field] = 'Price is too large';
  }
}

/**
 * Validate + normalize the seller-entered variant option groups.
 * Every group needs a unique name and at least one value; values are trimmed
 * and de-duplicated case-insensitively (first spelling wins).
 */
function normalizeVariants(
  variants: ProductVariant[],
  errors: Record<string, string>,
): ProductVariant[] {
  const out: ProductVariant[] = [];
  const seenNames = new Set<string>();

  for (const variant of variants) {
    const name = typeof variant?.name === 'string' ? variant.name.trim() : '';
    if (!name) {
      errors.variants = 'Every variant needs a name (for example "Size")';
      return out;
    }
    if (name.length > MAX_VARIANT_TEXT) {
      errors.variants = `Variant names must be ${MAX_VARIANT_TEXT} characters or fewer`;
      return out;
    }
    const nameKey = name.toLowerCase();
    if (seenNames.has(nameKey)) {
      errors.variants = `"${name}" is repeated â€” each variant name must be unique`;
      return out;
    }
    seenNames.add(nameKey);

    const rawValues = Array.isArray(variant.values) ? variant.values : [];
    const values: string[] = [];
    for (const raw of rawValues) {
      const value = typeof raw === 'string' ? raw.trim() : '';
      if (!value) continue;
      if (value.length > MAX_VARIANT_TEXT) {
        errors.variants = `Values for "${name}" must be ${MAX_VARIANT_TEXT} characters or fewer`;
        return out;
      }
      if (!values.some((existing) => existing.toLowerCase() === value.toLowerCase())) {
        values.push(value);
      }
    }
    if (values.length === 0) {
      errors.variants = `Add at least one value for "${name}" (for example "Small")`;
      return out;
    }
    if (values.length > MAX_VARIANT_VALUES) {
      errors.variants = `Each variant can have up to ${MAX_VARIANT_VALUES} values`;
      return out;
    }

    out.push({ name, values });
  }

  return out;
}

/** Validate + normalize a create/update payload. Returns only known fields. */
function sanitizeProductInput(
  data: CreateProductRequest,
  partial: boolean,
  errors: Record<string, string>,
): Record<string, unknown> {
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};

  if (!partial || data.name !== undefined) {
    const name = data.name?.trim() ?? '';
    if (!name || name.length > 120) errors.name = name ? 'Must be 120 characters or fewer' : 'Product name is required';
    else out.name = name;
  }
  if (data.description !== undefined) {
    checkText(data.description, 'description', 2000, errors);
    out.description = data.description?.trim() || null;
  }
  if (!partial || data.price !== undefined) {
    if (data.price === undefined || data.price === null) errors.price = 'Price is required';
    else checkPrice(data.price, 'price', errors);
    if (!errors.price) out.price = Math.round((data.price as number) * 100) / 100;
  }
  if (data.salePrice !== undefined) {
    checkPrice(data.salePrice, 'salePrice', errors);
    if (!errors.salePrice) out.salePrice = data.salePrice === null ? null : Math.round(data.salePrice * 100) / 100;
  }
  if (data.stock !== undefined) {
    if (data.stock === null) out.stock = null;
    else if (!Number.isInteger(data.stock) || data.stock < 0 || data.stock > 1_000_000) {
      errors.stock = 'Stock must be a whole number of 0 or more';
    } else out.stock = data.stock;
  }
  if (data.sku !== undefined) {
    checkText(data.sku, 'sku', 40, errors);
    out.sku = data.sku?.trim() || null;
  }
  // Delivery hub the product ships from. The Add Product page always sends the
  // platform default; `null` is accepted so a backend row can clear it, and the
  // UI then falls back to DEFAULT_DELIVERY_LOCATION when rendering.
  if (data.deliveryLocation !== undefined) {
    checkText(data.deliveryLocation, 'deliveryLocation', 120, errors);
    out.deliveryLocation = data.deliveryLocation?.trim() || null;
  }
  if (data.category !== undefined) {
    const category = data.category?.trim() || null;
    if (category && !(PRODUCT_CATEGORIES as readonly string[]).includes(category)) {
      errors.category = 'Unknown category';
    } else out.category = category;
  }
  if (data.status !== undefined) {
    if (data.status !== 'active' && data.status !== 'draft') errors.status = 'Status must be active or draft';
    else out.status = data.status;
  }
  if (data.imageUrl !== undefined) {
    const url = data.imageUrl;
    if (url && !/^(https?:\/\/|data:image\/)/.test(url)) {
      errors.imageUrl = 'Image must be an http(s) URL or an uploaded image';
    } else if (url && url.length > 500_000) {
      errors.imageUrl = 'Image is too large â€” use one under 5MB';
    } else out.imageUrl = url || null;
  }
  if (data.images !== undefined) {
    if (data.images === null) {
      out.images = null;
    } else if (!Array.isArray(data.images)) {
      errors.images = 'Images must be a list of URLs';
    } else if (data.images.length > 5) {
      errors.images = 'You can add up to 5 images';
    } else {
      const images = data.images.map((u) => u?.trim() || null);
      for (const url of images) {
        if (url && !/^(https?:\/\/|data:image\/)/.test(url)) {
          errors.images = 'Each image must be an http(s) URL or an uploaded image';
          break;
        }
        if (url && url.length > 500_000) {
          errors.images = 'An image is too large â€” use files under 5MB';
          break;
        }
      }
      if (!errors.images) {
        const cleanImages = images.filter((u): u is string => Boolean(u));
        out.images = cleanImages.length ? cleanImages : null;
      }
    }
  }
  if (data.imageAlt !== undefined) {
    checkText(data.imageAlt ?? undefined, 'imageAlt', 200, errors);
    out.imageAlt = data.imageAlt?.trim() || null;
  }
  if (data.variants !== undefined) {
    if (data.variants === null) {
      out.variants = null;
    } else if (!Array.isArray(data.variants)) {
      errors.variants = 'Variants must be a list of option groups';
    } else if (data.variants.length > MAX_VARIANTS) {
      errors.variants = `You can add up to ${MAX_VARIANTS} variants`;
    } else {
      const variants = normalizeVariants(data.variants, errors);
      if (!errors.variants) out.variants = variants.length ? variants : null;
    }
  }
  // Physical condition chosen by the seller ("Brand New" -> new, "Fairly
  // Used" -> used). Unknown values are rejected so the marketplace badge can
  // only ever render the two documented states.
  if (data.condition !== undefined) {
    if (data.condition !== null && data.condition !== 'new' && data.condition !== 'used') {
      errors.condition = 'Condition must be new or used';
    } else {
      out.condition = data.condition;
    }
  }
  // Marketplace featuring flag. `undefined` = field untouched (partial updates);
  // `null` is normalized to `false` so lists can filter with a plain boolean.
  if (data.featuredInMarketplace !== undefined) {
    if (data.featuredInMarketplace !== null && typeof data.featuredInMarketplace !== 'boolean') {
      errors.featuredInMarketplace = 'Featured must be true or false';
    } else {
      out.featuredInMarketplace = data.featuredInMarketplace === true;
    }
  }

  // Keep the denormalized cover in sync with the gallery: when the caller
  // provides `images` (but not an explicit `imageUrl`), the first image
  // becomes the cover.
  if (Array.isArray(out.images) && out.images.length > 0 && out.imageUrl === undefined) {
    out.imageUrl = out.images[0];
  }

  if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) failField(errors);
  return out;
}

/** Sale price must undercut the regular price (checks the merged result). */
function validateSalePrice(product: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  const price = product.price as number | undefined;
  const salePrice = product.salePrice as number | null | undefined;
  if (price !== undefined && salePrice !== null && salePrice !== undefined && salePrice >= price) {
    failField({ salePrice: 'Sale price must be lower than the regular price' });
  }
}

export class MockProductsApi implements ProductsApi {
  async getProducts(params: ProductQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Product>> {
    logApi('GET', '/products');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const viewer = await getSessionUserSafe();
      let items = mockDb.getCollection('products');

      if (params.sellerId) {
        items = items.filter((p) => p.sellerId === params.sellerId);
        // Full visibility ONLY for the owner's own workshop view; everyone
        // else (including anonymous visitors) sees just active products.
        const isOwnShop = viewer !== null && params.sellerId === viewer.id;
        if (!isOwnShop) items = items.filter((p) => p.status === 'active');
      } else {
        // Public catalog â€” drafts of ANY seller never leak, and only products
        // the seller chose to feature are listed (at most 2 per seller).
        // Everything else stays reachable via the seller's shop page.
        items = items.filter((p) => p.status === 'active');
        items = items.filter((p) => p.featuredInMarketplace === true);
      }
      items = [...items].sort(byNewestFirst);
      if (params.status) items = items.filter((p) => p.status === params.status);
      if (params.category) items = items.filter((p) => p.category === params.category);
      // Explicit featured filter (ProductQueryParams.featured). When omitted
      // the default visibility scoping above stays in charge.
      if (params.featured !== undefined) {
        items = items.filter((p) => p.featuredInMarketplace === params.featured);
      }
      if (params.search) {
        const q = params.search.toLowerCase();
        items = items.filter(
          (p) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.description?.toLowerCase().includes(q),
        );
      }

      const page = Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1);
      const pageSize = Math.min(200, Math.max(1, params.pageSize ?? 40));
      const total = items.length;
      const start = (page - 1) * pageSize;
      const paginated = items.slice(start, start + pageSize).map(withSellerProfile);

      return { items: paginated, total, page, pageSize };
    })());
  }

  /**
   * Opt-in aggregation â€” trivial for the mock (everything is in-memory), it
   * exists to satisfy the shared ProductsApi interface. Mirrors the real
   * adapter's contract: returns every matching item in one response.
   */
  async getAllProducts(params: ProductQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Product>> {
    logApi('GET', '/products?all');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const viewer = await getSessionUserSafe();
      let items = mockDb.getCollection('products');

      if (params.sellerId) {
        items = items.filter((p) => p.sellerId === params.sellerId);
        const isOwnShop = viewer !== null && params.sellerId === viewer.id;
        if (!isOwnShop) items = items.filter((p) => p.status === 'active');
      } else {
        items = items.filter((p) => p.status === 'active');
        items = items.filter((p) => p.featuredInMarketplace === true);
      }
      items = [...items].sort(byNewestFirst);
      if (params.status) items = items.filter((p) => p.status === params.status);
      if (params.category) items = items.filter((p) => p.category === params.category);
      if (params.featured !== undefined) {
        items = items.filter((p) => p.featuredInMarketplace === params.featured);
      }
      if (params.search) {
        const q = params.search.toLowerCase();
        items = items.filter(
          (p) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.description?.toLowerCase().includes(q),
        );
      }

      return {
        items: items.map(withSellerProfile),
        total: items.length,
        page: Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1),
        pageSize: items.length,
      };
    })());
  }

  async getProduct(id: string): Promise<Product> {
    logApi('GET', `/products/${id}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const product = mockDb.findById('products', id);
      if (!product) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Product not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      if (product.status === 'draft') {
        // Drafts are private to their owner â€” hide even their existence.
        const viewer = await getSessionUserSafe();
        if (!viewer || viewer.id !== product.sellerId) {
          throw new ApiError({ message: 'Product not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
        }
      }
      return withSellerProfile(product);
    })());
  }

  async createProduct(data: CreateProductRequest): Promise<Product> {
    logApi('POST', '/products');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      // Authentication REQUIRED â€” no more anonymous "unknown seller" products.
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const clean = sanitizeProductInput(data, false, {});
      validateSalePrice(clean);
      // The cap only applies to ACTIVE products â€” a featured draft can be
      // created freely; publishing it later re-runs the check (updateProduct).
      const createdIsActive = clean.status !== 'draft';
      // The workshop cap applies to ALL products (active + drafts combined).
      enforceWorkshopLimit(user.id);
      enforceListingLimit(user.id, null, clean.featuredInMarketplace === true && createdIsActive);
      const timestamp = nowIso();
      return mockDb.insert('products', {
        id: generateId(),
        sellerId: user.id,
        seller: user.fullName,
        ...clean,
        rating: 0,
        reviews: 0,
        createdAt: timestamp,
        updatedAt: timestamp,
      } as never);
    })());
  }

  async updateProduct(id: string, data: UpdateProductRequest): Promise<Product> {
    logApi('PATCH', `/products/${id}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const existing = mockDb.findById('products', id);
      if (!existing || existing.sellerId !== user.id) {
        // OWNERSHIP ENFORCEMENT â€” 404 (not 403) to prevent id enumeration.
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Product not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      const clean = sanitizeProductInput(data as CreateProductRequest, true, {});
      const merged = { ...existing, ...clean };
      validateSalePrice(merged);
      // Cap applies whenever the MERGED product is a featured active product
      // and it was not already counted as one (so un-featuring stays allowed).
      const alreadyFeaturedActive = existing.featuredInMarketplace === true && existing.status === 'active';
      const willBeFeatured = merged.featuredInMarketplace === true && merged.status === 'active';
      if (willBeFeatured && !alreadyFeaturedActive) {
        enforceListingLimit(user.id, id, true);
      }
      const updated = mockDb.update('products', id, clean);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Product not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      return updated as Product;
    })());
  }

  async deleteProduct(id: string): Promise<void> {
    logApi('DELETE', `/products/${id}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const existing = mockDb.findById('products', id);
      if (!existing || existing.sellerId !== user.id) {
        // OWNERSHIP ENFORCEMENT â€” nobody can delete another seller's product.
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Product not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      mockDb.remove('products', id);
    })());
  }
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\mock\security.ts =====

/**
 * Security primitives for the mock API layer.
 *
 * The mock backend simulates the security posture a REAL backend must have:
 *
 * - Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (120k iterations, per-user
 *   random salt) via the Web Crypto API â€” never stored or logged in plaintext.
 * - Session tokens are 256-bit CSPRNG values (crypto.getRandomValues) and are
 *   stored in the "database" only as SHA-256 hashes, exactly like a real
 *   backend would never persist raw token strings.
 * - Password verification is constant-time (timing-safe comparison).
 *
 * These functions are async because Web Crypto is async; the seed database
 * ships pre-computed hashes (generated with the identical PBKDF2 parameters)
 * so database loading stays synchronous.
 */

const PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 120_000;
const SALT_BYTES = 16;
const HASH_BYTES = 32;

function toBase64(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  let binary = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) binary += String.fromCharCode(bytes[i]);
  return btoa(binary);
}

function fromBase64(value: string): Uint8Array {
  const binary = atob(value);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}

function subtle(): SubtleCrypto {
  if (typeof crypto === 'undefined' || !crypto.subtle) {
    throw new Error('Web Crypto API is required for password hashing.');
  }
  return crypto.subtle;
}

/** Cryptographically secure, URL-safe opaque token (256-bit by default). */
export function generateSecureToken(byteLength = 32): string {
  const bytes = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(byteLength));
  return toBase64(bytes).replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');
}

/** SHA-256 hex digest â€” used to store/lookup session tokens without keeping raw values. */
export async function sha256Hex(value: string): Promise<string> {
  const digest = await subtle().digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(value));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(digest))
    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
    .join('');
}

async function deriveBits(
  password: string,
  salt: Uint8Array,
  iterations: number,
  lengthBytes: number,
): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const keyMaterial = await subtle().importKey(
    'raw',
    new TextEncoder().encode(password),
    'PBKDF2',
    false,
    ['deriveBits'],
  );
  const bits = await subtle().deriveBits(
    { name: 'PBKDF2', salt: salt as BufferSource, iterations, hash: 'SHA-256' },
    keyMaterial,
    lengthBytes * 8,
  );
  return new Uint8Array(bits);
}

/** Hash a password for storage. Format: pbkdf2$<iterations>$<saltB64>$<hashB64>. */
export async function hashPassword(password: string): Promise<string> {
  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(SALT_BYTES));
  const hash = await deriveBits(password, salt, PBKDF2_ITERATIONS, HASH_BYTES);
  return `pbkdf2$${PBKDF2_ITERATIONS}$${toBase64(salt)}$${toBase64(hash)}`;
}

/** Verify a password against a stored pbkdf2$ hash (constant-time comparison). */
export async function verifyPassword(password: string, stored: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const parts = stored.split('$');
    if (parts.length !== 4 || parts[0] !== 'pbkdf2') return false;
    const iterations = Number.parseInt(parts[1], 10);
    if (!Number.isFinite(iterations) || iterations <= 0) return false;
    const salt = fromBase64(parts[2]);
    const expected = fromBase64(parts[3]);
    const actual = await deriveBits(password, salt, iterations, expected.length);
    return timingSafeEqual(actual, expected);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** Length-independent, constant-time byte comparison. */
export function timingSafeEqual(a: Uint8Array, b: Uint8Array): boolean {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  let diff = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) diff |= a[i] ^ b[i];
  return diff === 0;
}

/** Small blocklist of the most-broken passwords â€” checked on register/change. */
const COMMON_PASSWORDS = new Set([
  'password',
  'password1',
  'password123',
  '12345678',
  '123456789',
  '1234567890',
  'qwerty123',
  'qwertyuiop',
  'iloveyou1',
  'admin1234',
  'letmein12',
  'welcome1',
  'abc12345',
  '11111111',
  '12341234',
  'sunshine1',
  'princess1',
  'football1',
]);

export interface PasswordPolicyResult {
  ok: boolean;
  error?: string;
}

/**
 * Server-side password policy (defense in depth â€” the UI validates too, but
 * the API never trusts the client).
 */
export function validatePasswordStrength(password: string): PasswordPolicyResult {
  if (!password || password.length < 8) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Password must be at least 8 characters' };
  }
  if (password.length > 128) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Password must be at most 128 characters' };
  }
  if (!/[a-zA-Z]/.test(password) || !/[0-9]/.test(password)) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Password must contain at least one letter and one number' };
  }
  if (COMMON_PASSWORDS.has(password.toLowerCase())) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'This password is too common. Please choose a stronger one' };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

/**
 * Server-side session guard for the mock API.
 *
 * Every protected mock endpoint resolves the caller through requireSession(),
 * which behaves like real backend middleware:
 *
 *  1. Reads the Bearer (access) token from the session store.
 *  2. Looks the token up by its SHA-256 hash â€” raw tokens are never stored.
 *  3. Enforces access-token expiry (401 when expired).
 *  4. Verifies the user still exists and is active (401/403 otherwise).
 *
 * This is the single choke point that makes "user A can never read or mutate
 * user B's data" true at the API layer â€” components cannot bypass it because
 * they never touch the database directly.
 */
import { mockDb } from './mockDatabase';
import type { MockSession, StoredUser } from './mockDatabase';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { sessionStore } from '../session';
import { sha256Hex } from './security';

export interface AuthContext {
  user: StoredUser;
  session: MockSession;
}

function unauthorized(message: string): ApiError {
  return new ApiError({ message, status: 401, code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' });
}

/** Require a valid, unexpired session. Throws ApiError(401/403) otherwise. */
export async function requireSession(): Promise<AuthContext> {
  const token = sessionStore.getAccessToken();
  if (!token) {
    throw unauthorized('Not authenticated. Please log in.');
  }
  const tokenHash = await sha256Hex(token);
  const session = mockDb.query('sessions', (s) => s.accessTokenHash === tokenHash)[0];
  if (!session) {
    throw unauthorized('Session expired. Please log in again.');
  }
  if (session.accessExpiresAt <= Date.now()) {
    throw unauthorized('Session expired. Please log in again.');
  }
  const user = mockDb.findById('users', session.userId);
  if (!user) {
    throw unauthorized('This account no longer exists.');
  }
  if (user.status !== 'active') {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'This account has been suspended.',
      status: 403,
      code: 'FORBIDDEN',
    });
  }
  return { user, session };
}

/**
 * Non-throwing variant for endpoints that are public but behave differently
 * for a signed-in user (e.g. product listings). Returns null when anonymous.
 */
export async function getSessionUserSafe(): Promise<StoredUser | null> {
  try {
    return (await requireSession()).user;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
