/* --------------------------- Personalization layer ------------------------ */

/** Map a free-form product category string to a storefront bucket. */
function toBucket(category?: string | null): StorefrontCategory {
  const c = (category ?? '').toLowerCase();
  if (/tech|electronic|gadget|phone|laptop|computer|device|accessor/.test(c)) return 'tech';
  if (/campus|school|book|station|study|supplie/.test(c)) return 'campus';
  return 'lifestyle';
}

/** Stable pseudo-number from a string (for demo store IDs). */
function hashish(value: string): number {
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i += 1) h = (h * 31 + value.charCodeAt(i)) % 1000000;
  return h;
}

/** "07051917468" -> "https://wa.me/2347051917468" */
function toWhatsappUrl(phone?: string | null): string {
  const digits = (phone ?? '').replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (!digits) return 'https://wa.me/2347051917468';
  const local = digits.startsWith('0') ? digits.slice(1) : digits;
  return `https://wa.me/234${local}`;
}

/** "â‚¦1,249.50" style â€” the marketplace prices in Nigerian Naira. */
function ngn(value: number): string {
  return `â‚¦${Math.round(value).toLocaleString('en-US')}`;
}

/**
 * Build the storefront for a REGISTERED seller whose store-name slug matches.
 * Their active products become the catalog; demo imagery/annotations fill any
 * gaps so the layout of the original mockup is always fully represented.
 */
function buildPersonalizedStore(
  slug: string,
  profile: {
    storeName?: string | null; school?: string | null; phone?: string | null;
    logoUrl?: string | null; bannerUrl?: string | null; userId: string; id: string;
    storeTemplate?: string | null; bannerImages?: string[] | null; pickupLocation?: string | null; supportEmail?: string | null;
  },
  ownerName: string,
  ownerEmail: string,
  memberSinceIso?: string | null,
  ownerProducts?: Array<{
    id: string; name: string; description?: string | null; price: number | null; salePrice?: number | null;
    stock?: number | null; category?: string | null; imageUrl?: string | null; imageAlt?: string | null; images?: string[] | null;
    variants?: Array<{ name: string; values: string[] }> | null;
    rating: number | null; reviews: number | null;
  }>,
): Storefront {
  const name = (profile.storeName || ownerName || 'My Store').trim();
  const products = (ownerProducts ?? []).map((p, index) => {
    const bucket = toBucket(p.category);
    const listPrice = p.price ?? 0;
    const onSale = p.salePrice != null && p.salePrice < listPrice;
    const images = p.images?.length ? p.images : (p.imageUrl ? [p.imageUrl] : [FALLBACK_IMAGES[index % FALLBACK_IMAGES.length]]);
    return {
      id: `sf-${p.id}`,
      name: p.name,
      description: p.description || p.name,
      category: bucket,
      categoryLabel: CATEGORY_LABELS[bucket],
      price: Math.round(onSale ? p.salePrice! : listPrice),
      priceLabel: ngn(onSale ? p.salePrice! : listPrice),
      oldPriceLabel: onSale ? ngn(listPrice) : null,
      rating: p.rating || 4.9,
      reviews: p.reviews || 0,
      popularity: p.reviews || Math.round((p.rating || 4.9) * 20),
      stock: p.stock ?? null,
      badge: onSale ? ('flash' as const) : null,
      campusPickup: bucket === 'campus',
      image: images[0],
      imageAlt: p.imageAlt || p.name,
      images,
      variants: p.variants?.length
        ? p.variants.map((variant) => ({ name: variant.name, values: [...variant.values] }))
        : undefined,
    } satisfies StorefrontProduct;
  });

  const rated = products.filter((p) => p.reviews > 0);
  const avgRating = rated.length > 0 ? rated.reduce((s, p) => s + p.rating, 0) / rated.length : 4.9;
  const totalReviews = products.reduce((s, p) => s + p.reviews, 0);
  const counts = {
    all: products.length,
    tech: products.filter((p) => p.category === 'tech').length,
    campus: products.filter((p) => p.category === 'campus').length,
    lifestyle: products.filter((p) => p.category === 'lifestyle').length,
  };
  const year = memberSinceIso ? new Date(memberSinceIso).getFullYear() : new Date().getFullYear();
  // Branding uploaded by the seller â€” null means the storefront renders the
  // store NAME as its logo and cover until the seller uploads real artwork.
  const logoImage = profile.logoUrl || null;
  const bannerImage = profile.bannerUrl || null;
  const bannerImages = profile.bannerImages?.length ? profile.bannerImages : (bannerImage ? [bannerImage] : []);

  return {
    ...buildDemoStore(),
    slug,
    name,
    owner: ownerName || 'Seller',
    school: profile.school || 'Olabisi Onabanjo University',
    storeId: `#${(slugifyStoreName(name).slice(0, 2) || 'ST').toUpperCase()}-${9000 + (hashish(profile.userId) % 999)}`,
    // Real seller id so the storefront page can fetch this seller's catalog
    // through the products API when the mock embeds none.
    sellerId: profile.userId,
    rating: Math.round(avgRating * 10) / 10,
    reviewCount: Math.max(totalReviews, 1),
    domain: getPrettyStoreDomain(slug),
    whatsappUrl: toWhatsappUrl(profile.phone),
    phone: profile.phone || '07051917468',
    email: profile.supportEmail || ownerEmail,
    template: profile.storeTemplate ?? null,
    pickupLocation: profile.pickupLocation ?? null,
    memberSinceLabel: `Since ${year}`,
    bioLead: `Run by ${ownerName || 'an independent seller'}, a student merchant at ${profile.school || 'Olabisi Onabanjo University'}. ${name} was launched to eliminate the hassle of waiting days for Lagos deliveries.`,
    bioDetail:
      'Every product is hand-tested, stocked directly on campus, and backed with peer escrow verification. We prioritize verified campus distribution points for zero shipping stress.',
    bannerImage,
    bannerImages,
    bannerAlt: profile.bannerUrl ? `${name} storefront cover` : undefined,
    avatarImage: logoImage,
    avatarAlt: profile.logoUrl ? `${name} logo` : undefined,
    reviewsNote: `All ${Math.max(totalReviews, 1).toLocaleString('en-US')} reviews verified with on-chain campus pickup receipts`,
    catalogCounts: counts,
    products,
  };
}

export class MockStorefrontApi implements StorefrontApi {
  async getStorefront(slugRaw: string): Promise<Storefront> {
    logApi('GET', `/storefront/${slugRaw || 'globalstore'}`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const slug = slugifyStoreName(slugRaw);
      if (!slug || slug === 'globalstore' || slug === 'demo' || slug === 'store') {
        return buildDemoStore();
      }

      // Find a registered seller whose domain slugifies to this slug. The
      // dashboard derives the domain from storeName when set, else the owner's
      // full name (getStoreDisplayName), so both are matched here.
      const byStoreName = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (p) => slugifyStoreName(p.storeName ?? '') === slug);
      const byOwnerName = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (p) => {
        if (p.storeName && p.storeName.trim()) return false; // storeName takes priority
        const owners = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.id === p.userId);
        return slugifyStoreName(owners[0]?.fullName ?? '') === slug;
      });
      const profiles = [...byStoreName, ...byOwnerName];
      if (profiles.length === 0) {
        // Public mock mode must remain viewable even when a seller was created
        // outside this browser's local mock database.
        const fallback = buildDemoStore();
        return {
          ...fallback,
          slug,
          domain: getPrettyStoreDomain(slug),
        };
      }

      const profile = profiles[0];
      const owners = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.id === profile.userId);
      const owner = owners[0];
      const products = mockDb.query('products', (p) => p.sellerId === profile.userId && p.status === 'active');

      if (!owner || products.length === 0) {
        // Registered but nothing published yet â†’ demo store with their identity.
        return buildPersonalizedStore(slug, profile, owner?.fullName ?? 'Seller', owner?.email ?? 'seller@universe.market', owner?.createdAt ?? null, []);
      }

      return buildPersonalizedStore(slug, profile, owner.fullName, owner.email, owner.createdAt, products);
    })());
  }
}

/**
 * Mock Uploads API â€” simulates image upload endpoints for development.
 *
 * The "upload" is the same client-side compression the product forms already
 * use (lib/image.js); the returned data URL stands in for the URL a real
 * backend would return from POST /uploads/images. Success here means the
 * local compression worked â€” which is exactly why the REAL adapter (and the
 * contract) insist on backend-confirmed success.
 */
import type { UploadedFile } from '../types';
import type { UploadsApi } from '../services/uploads';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';

export class MockUploadsApi implements UploadsApi {
  async uploadImage(file: File): Promise<UploadedFile> {
    logApi('POST', '/uploads/images');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      try {
        const url = await fileToCompressedDataUrl(file);
        return { url, name: file.name, size: file.size };

        throw new ApiError({
          message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not process that image.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { image: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Invalid image' },
        });
      }
    })());

/**
 * Mock Users API â€” implements the UsersApi contract against the mock DB.
 *
 * Security notes:
 * - Every method requires a valid session (requireSession() guard).
 * - updateCurrentUser() uses a strict field WHITELIST â€” client input can never
 *   touch email, passwordHash, accountType, status or role (mass-assignment
 *   protection).
 * - Sensitive operations (password change, email change, account deletion)
 *   require the CURRENT PASSWORD and feed failed confirmations into the same
 *   brute-force lockout as login.
 * - Account deletion cascades: products, seller profile and every session are
 *   removed with the user.
 */
import type {
  ChangePasswordRequest,
  DeleteAccountRequest,
  PublicSellerProfile,
  SellerProfile,
  UpdateEmailRequest,
  UpdateSellerProfileRequest,
  UpdateUserRequest,
  User,
} from '../types';
import type { UsersApi } from '../services/users';
import { mockDb, generateId, nowIso } from './mockDatabase';
import type { StoredUser } from './mockDatabase';
import { withMockLatency } from './mockLatency';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';
import { sessionStore } from '../session';
import { requireSession } from './sessionGuard';
import { hashPassword, validatePasswordStrength, verifyPassword } from './security';
import { isKnownStoreTemplate } from '../../lib/storeTemplates';

function toPublicUser(stored: StoredUser): User {
  const { passwordHash: _p, failedLoginCount: _f, lockedUntil: _l, ...publicUser } = stored;
  return publicUser;
}

/** Shared password confirmation with lockout for destructive operations. */
async function assertCurrentPassword(user: StoredUser, currentPassword: string): Promise<void> {
  const ok = await verifyPassword(currentPassword ?? '', user.passwordHash);
  if (!ok) {
    // Count toward brute-force lockout, same as a failed login.
    const count = (user.failedLoginCount ?? 0) + 1;
    const lockedUntil = count >= 5 ? Date.now() + 15 * 60 * 1000 : null;
    mockDb.update('users', user.id, { failedLoginCount: count, lockedUntil } as never);
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'Your current password is incorrect.',
      status: 401,
      code: 'INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD',
      fieldErrors: { currentPassword: 'Incorrect password' },
    });
  }
}

/** Truncate helper â€” returns undefined for empty/undefined input. */
function optionalText(value: string | undefined | null, max: number): string | undefined | null {
  if (value === undefined) return undefined;
  if (value === null) return null;
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return null;
  return trimmed.slice(0, max);
}

/**
 * Image-field sanitizer (store logo / cover picture).
 * Accepts http(s) URLs or compressed data URLs only, with a hard size cap â€”
 * the same rules the products API applies to product images.
 */
function optionalImage(value: string | undefined | null): string | null | undefined {
  if (value === undefined) return undefined;
  if (value === null) return null;
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return null;
  if (!/^(https?:\/\/|data:image\/)/.test(trimmed)) return undefined;
  if (trimmed.length > 500_000) return undefined;
  return trimmed;
}

export class MockUsersApi implements UsersApi {
  async getSellerProfile(): Promise<SellerProfile> {
    logApi('GET', '/users/me/seller-profile');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      const profiles = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (p) => p.userId === user.id);
      if (profiles.length === 0) {
        // Auto-create a profile on first read so the UI always has something.
        const timestamp = nowIso();
        return mockDb.insert('sellerProfiles', {
          id: generateId(),
          userId: user.id,
          storeName: null,
          phone: null,
          level: null,
          department: null,
          course: null,
          school: null,
          bio: null,
          createdAt: timestamp,
          updatedAt: timestamp,
        } as never);
      }
      return profiles[0];
    })());
  }

  /**
   * PUBLIC seller profile â€” deliberately session-free (marketplace visitors are
   * anonymous). Read-only: only seller-PUBLISHED fields are returned, and an
   * unknown id or a buyer account is a real 404 so the UI can show "seller not
   * found" instead of an empty shell.
   */
  async getPublicSellerProfile(sellerId: string): Promise<PublicSellerProfile> {
    logApi('GET', `/users/${sellerId}/seller-profile`);
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const seller = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.id === sellerId && u.accountType === 'seller')[0];
      if (!seller) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Seller not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      const profile = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (p) => p.userId === seller.id)[0];
      // Store name first, account name as the documented fallback â€” never a
      // prefilled demo value.
      return {
        userId: seller.id,
        name: profile?.storeName || seller.fullName || 'Campus Seller',
        email: seller.email || null,
        phone: profile?.phone ?? seller.phone ?? null,
        level: profile?.level ?? null,
        department: profile?.department ?? null,
        course: profile?.course ?? null,
        school: profile?.school ?? null,
        bio: profile?.bio ?? null,
        logoUrl: profile?.logoUrl ?? seller.avatarUrl ?? null,
      };
    })());
  }

  async updateSellerProfile(data: UpdateSellerProfileRequest): Promise<SellerProfile> {
    logApi('PATCH', '/users/me/seller-profile');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      // Whitelist + sanitize every field (length caps, trimming). Values are
      // typed loosely because the patch mixes strings with the bannerImages
      // array (image fields are validated separately below).
      const patch: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      if (data.storeName !== undefined) patch.storeName = optionalText(data.storeName, 80) ?? null;
      if (data.phone !== undefined) patch.phone = optionalText(data.phone, 20) ?? null;
      if (data.level !== undefined) patch.level = optionalText(data.level, 10) ?? null;
      if (data.department !== undefined) patch.department = optionalText(data.department, 80) ?? null;
      if (data.course !== undefined) patch.course = optionalText(data.course, 120) ?? null;
      if (data.school !== undefined) patch.school = optionalText(data.school, 120) ?? null;
      if (data.bio !== undefined) patch.bio = optionalText(data.bio, 1000) ?? null;
      if (data.logoUrl !== undefined) patch.logoUrl = optionalImage(data.logoUrl) ?? null;
      if (data.bannerUrl !== undefined) patch.bannerUrl = optionalImage(data.bannerUrl) ?? null;
      if (data.bannerImages !== undefined) {
        const images = Array.isArray(data.bannerImages)
          ? data.bannerImages.map((image) => optionalImage(image)).filter((image): image is string => Boolean(image)).slice(0, 5)
          : [];
        patch.bannerImages = images.length ? images : null;
        if (data.bannerUrl === undefined) patch.bannerUrl = images[0] ?? null;
      }
      if (data.storeTemplate !== undefined) {
        // Whitelist against the registered storefront templates â€” unknown or
        // empty values reset to null (the classic boutique look).
        patch.storeTemplate =
          data.storeTemplate && isKnownStoreTemplate(data.storeTemplate) ? data.storeTemplate : null;
      }
      if (data.pickupLocation !== undefined) {
        patch.pickupLocation = optionalText(data.pickupLocation, 120) ?? null;
      }
      if (data.supportEmail !== undefined) {
        patch.supportEmail = optionalText(data.supportEmail, 120) ?? null;
      }

      const profiles = mockDb.query('sellerProfiles', (p) => p.userId === user.id);
      if (profiles.length === 0) {
        const timestamp = nowIso();
        return mockDb.insert('sellerProfiles', {
          id: generateId(),
          userId: user.id,
          ...patch,
          createdAt: timestamp,
          updatedAt: timestamp,
        } as never);
      }
      const updated = mockDb.update('sellerProfiles', profiles[0].id, patch as never);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'Profile not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      return updated as SellerProfile;
    })());
  }


  async updateCurrentUser(data: UpdateUserRequest): Promise<User> {
    logApi('PATCH', '/users/me');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      // MASS-ASSIGNMENT PROTECTION: build the patch from a strict whitelist.
      // Email, password, accountType and status can NEVER be changed here.
      // Phone/avatar also accept null ("clear the value") even though
      // UpdateUserRequest only exposes string â€” the DB row stores nulls.
      const patch: Partial<Omit<UpdateUserRequest, 'phone' | 'avatarUrl'>> & {
        phone?: string | null;
        avatarUrl?: string | null;
      } = {};
      if (data.fullName !== undefined) {
        const fullName = data.fullName.trim();
        if (fullName && (fullName.length < 2 || fullName.length > 80)) {
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
            status: 422,
            code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
            fieldErrors: { fullName: 'Full name must be between 2 and 80 characters' },
          });
        }
        if (fullName) patch.fullName = fullName;
      }
      if (data.phone !== undefined) {
        const phone = data.phone?.trim() ?? '';
        if (phone && !/^[+()\d\s-]{1,20}$/.test(phone)) {
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
            status: 422,
            code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
            fieldErrors: { phone: 'Enter a valid phone number' },
          });
        }
        patch.phone = phone || null;
      }
      if (data.avatarUrl !== undefined) {
        const url = data.avatarUrl;
        if (url && !/^(https?:\/\/|data:image\/)/.test(url)) {
          throw new ApiError({
            message: 'Please correct the highlighted fields.',
            status: 422,
            code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
            fieldErrors: { avatarUrl: 'Avatar must be a http(s) or image data URL' },
          });
        }
        patch.avatarUrl = url && url.length <= 500_000 ? url : null;
      }

      const updated = mockDb.update('users', user.id, patch as never);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'User not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      return toPublicUser(updated as StoredUser);
    })());
  }

  async changePassword(data: ChangePasswordRequest): Promise<void> {
    logApi('PATCH', '/users/me/password');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user, session } = await requireSession();
      await assertCurrentPassword(user, data.currentPassword);

      const policy = validatePasswordStrength(data.newPassword ?? '');
      if (!policy.ok) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please choose a stronger password.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'WEAK_PASSWORD',
          fieldErrors: { newPassword: policy.error ?? 'Password does not meet the requirements' },
        });
      }

      mockDb.update('users', user.id, {
        passwordHash: await hashPassword(data.newPassword),
        failedLoginCount: 0,
        lockedUntil: null,
      } as never);

      // SECURITY: revoke every OTHER session (e.g. an old laptop that is still
      // signed in) but keep the current device signed in.
      mockDb
        .query('sessions', (s) => s.userId === user.id && s.id !== session.id)
        .forEach((s) => mockDb.remove('sessions', s.id));
    })());
  }

  async updateEmail(data: UpdateEmailRequest): Promise<User> {
    logApi('POST', '/users/me/email');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      await assertCurrentPassword(user, data.currentPassword);

      const newEmail = data.newEmail?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      if (!newEmail || !/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(newEmail) || newEmail.length > 254) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Please enter a valid email address.',
          status: 422,
          code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
          fieldErrors: { newEmail: 'Enter a valid email' },
        });
      }
      const taken = mockDb.query('users', (u) => u.email === newEmail && u.id !== user.id);
      if (taken.length > 0) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'That email is already in use.',
          status: 409,
          code: 'EMAIL_TAKEN',
          fieldErrors: { newEmail: 'Email is already registered' },
        });
      }

      const updated = mockDb.update('users', user.id, { email: newEmail } as never);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new ApiError({ message: 'User not found.', status: 404, code: 'NOT_FOUND' });
      }
      return toPublicUser(updated as StoredUser);
    })());
  }

  async deleteAccount(data: DeleteAccountRequest): Promise<void> {
    logApi('DELETE', '/users/me');
    return withMockLatency((async () => {
      const { user } = await requireSession();
      await assertCurrentPassword(user, data.currentPassword);

      // CASCADE: remove everything the account owns, then the account itself.
      mockDb
        .query('products', (p) => p.sellerId === user.id)
        .forEach((p) => mockDb.remove('products', p.id));
      mockDb
        .query('sellerProfiles', (p) => p.userId === user.id)
        .forEach((p) => mockDb.remove('sellerProfiles', p.id));
      mockDb
        .query('sessions', (s) => s.userId === user.id)
        .forEach((s) => mockDb.remove('sessions', s.id));
      mockDb.remove('users', user.id);
      sessionStore.clear();
    })());
  }
}

/**
 * Barrel for the centralized backend-response normalizers.
 *
 * Every Real*Api implementation imports from here so dialect handling
 * (snake_case, envelopes, numeric strings, DRF pagination) lives in exactly
 * one place. The mock API does NOT use these â€” it emits contract-shaped data
 * directly.
 */
export * from './primitives';
export * from './product';
export * from './user';

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\normalize\primitives.ts =====

/**
 * Shared primitive normalizers for the REAL backend adapter.
 *
 * This is the ONE place where "backend dialect" differences are translated:
 *
 * - snake_case / kebab-case keys  -> camelCase (`sale_price` -> `salePrice`)
 * - `{ data: ... }` envelopes     -> unwrapped
 * - numeric strings               -> numbers where the contract type needs one
 * - empty strings / null          -> null (never a fabricated default)
 *
 * SCOPE GUARANTEE: these helpers only reshape data the backend actually sent.
 * None of them invent business values â€” every field the backend omits stays
 * `null`/`undefined` and the UI renders its missing-data state.
 */

/** True for a JSON object (never for arrays or null). */
export function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/** "featured_in_marketplace" -> "featuredInMarketplace" (camel keys pass through). */
export function camelizeKey(key: string): string {
  if (!/[_-]/.test(key)) return key;
  const [head, ...rest] = key.split(/[_-]+/).filter(Boolean);
  if (head === undefined) return key;
  return head + rest.map((part) => part.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + part.slice(1)).join('');
}

/** Deep key transform. Object keys are camelized; values are never modified. */
export function camelizeDeep<T = unknown>(value: unknown): T {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((entry) => camelizeDeep(entry)) as T;
  if (!isRecord(value)) return value as T;
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [key, entry] of Object.entries(value)) out[camelizeKey(key)] = camelizeDeep(entry);
  return out as T;
}

/**
 * First present alias for a field, so a backend that names things slightly
 * differently (`title` vs `name`, `image` vs `imageUrl`) still works.
 *
 * This leniency is limited to documented aliases per endpoint in
 * docs/API_CONTRACT.md â€” it is not an invitation to accept arbitrary shapes.
 */
export function pick(record: Record<string, unknown>, keys: string[]): unknown {
  for (const key of keys) {
    const value = record[key];
    if (value !== undefined && value !== null) return value;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/** Unwrap `{ data: X }` / `{ product: X }` / `{ user: X }` style envelopes. */
export function unwrapEnvelope(raw: unknown, keys: string[]): unknown {
  if (!isRecord(raw)) return raw;
  for (const key of keys) {
    const value = raw[key];
    if (value !== undefined && value !== null) return value;
  }
  return raw;
}

/**
 * Lenient numeric parse â€” accepts 12, "12", "309985.00", "â‚¦1,249.50".
 *
 * DERIVATION RULE: converting a numeric STRING the backend sent into a number
 * is normalization. Returning a number the backend never sent is fabrication â€”
 * callers must use `null` for that instead.
 */
export function toNumber(value: unknown): number | null {
  if (typeof value === 'number') return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null;
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    const cleaned = value.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, '');
    if (!cleaned || cleaned === '-' || cleaned === '.') return null;
    const parsed = Number(cleaned);
    return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : null;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Trimmed non-empty string, or null. */
export function toText(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    const trimmed = value.trim();
    return trimmed ? trimmed : null;
  }
  if (typeof value === 'number' || typeof value === 'boolean') return String(value);
  return null;
}

/** Lenient boolean parse ("true" / 1 / "yes" -> true). Null when absent. */
export function toBoolean(value: unknown): boolean | null {
  if (typeof value === 'boolean') return value;
  if (typeof value === 'number') return value !== 0;
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (['true', '1', 'yes', 'y', 'on'].includes(normalized)) return true;
    if (['false', '0', 'no', 'n', 'off', ''].includes(normalized)) return false;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Array of trimmed non-empty strings (never null). */
export function toStringArray(value: unknown): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return [];
  return value.map((entry) => toText(entry)).filter((entry): entry is string => Boolean(entry));
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\normalize\product.ts =====

/**
 * Product normalizers â€” backend payload -> the UI's `Product` contract.
 *
 * FABRICATION RULES (see docs/API_CONTRACT.md):
 * - `price`, `salePrice`, `stock` are only ever numbers the backend sent.
 *   A missing price is `null` (rendered as "â€”" by the UI), never 0 â€” 0 would
 *   present the product as free.
 * - `rating` / `reviews` are review data the backend owns. The frontend never
 *   invents them; a product without reviews is `null`, not 4.9.
 * - `status` is the ONE documented display default: when the backend returns a
 *   product row from a list/detail endpoint it is meant to be visible, so a
 *   missing `status` is treated as "active". The real backend must always send
 *   `status` (contract requirement); this default only protects rendering.
 */
import type {
  PaginatedResponse,
  Product,
  ProductStatus,
  ProductVariant,
} from '../types';
import {
  isRecord,
  pick,
  toBoolean,
  toNumber,
  toText,
  toStringArray,
} from './primitives';

const MAX_VARIANTS = 10;
const MAX_VARIANT_VALUES = 20;

/**
 * Normalize the seller-attested physical condition. Accepts the documented
 * values plus the common spellings a backend might send ("brand_new",
 * "fairly_used", "pre-owned"); anything unrecognized is `null` â€” the UI then
 * shows "Condition unavailable" rather than inventing a state.
 */
export function normalizeCondition(value: unknown): 'new' | 'used' | null {
  const text = toText(value);
  if (!text) return null;
  const key = text.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, '_');
  if (key === 'new' || key === 'brand_new' || key === 'brandnew') return 'new';
  if (key === 'used' || key === 'fairly_used' || key === 'fairlyused' || key === 'preowned' || key === 'pre_owned' || key === 'second_hand') return 'used';
  return null;
}

/** Normalize variant option groups (Size â†’ Small/Medium). Null when there are none. */
export function normalizeVariants(value: unknown): ProductVariant[] | null {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return null;
  const groups: ProductVariant[] = [];
  for (const entry of value) {
    if (!isRecord(entry)) continue;
    const name = toText(pick(entry, ['name', 'option', 'label', 'title']));
    if (!name) continue;
    const values = toStringArray(pick(entry, ['values', 'options', 'choices', 'items']));
    if (values.length === 0) continue;
    groups.push({ name, values: values.slice(0, MAX_VARIANT_VALUES) });
    if (groups.length >= MAX_VARIANTS) break;
  }
  return groups.length > 0 ? groups : null;
}

/** Normalize category values returned either as text or as a related object. */
function normalizeCategory(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  const text = toText(value);
  if (text) return text;
  if (!isRecord(value)) return undefined;
  return toText(pick(value, ['name', 'label', 'title', 'value', 'category'])) ?? undefined;
}

/**
 * Normalize one product payload into the UI's `Product` shape.
 *
 * Guarantees everything the marketplace reads without null checks:
 * - numeric `salePrice` / `stock` (backends commonly serialize decimals as
 *   strings â€” that conversion is normalization, not fabrication),
 * - a real boolean `featuredInMarketplace` (absent = false: the seller has not
 *   opted in, which is the honest default and the conservative one),
 * - `images[0]` mirrored into `imageUrl` so cards and galleries never render
 *   empty when the backend only sends the gallery array (documented
 *   denormalization, the mock API stores the same redundancy).
 */
export function normalizeProduct(raw: unknown): Product {
  const record = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
  const images = toStringArray(pick(record, ['images', 'gallery', 'photos', 'imageUrls']));
  const explicitCover = toText(pick(record, ['imageUrl', 'image', 'coverImage', 'thumbnail', 'photo']));
  const cover = explicitCover ?? images[0] ?? null;
  const status: ProductStatus = toText(pick(record, ['status', 'state'])) === 'draft' ? 'draft' : 'active';
  const createdAt = toText(pick(record, ['createdAt', 'created', 'dateCreated'])) ?? '';
  const gallery = cover && !images.includes(cover) ? [cover, ...images] : images;

  return {
    id: toText(pick(record, ['id', 'uuid', 'productId', '_id'])) ?? '',
    sellerId: toText(pick(record, ['sellerId', 'ownerId', 'userId', 'storeId'])) ?? '',
    seller: toText(pick(record, ['seller', 'sellerName', 'storeName', 'shopName'])),
    sellerLogo: toText(pick(record, ['sellerLogo', 'sellerLogoUrl', 'storeLogo', 'storeLogoUrl', 'logoUrl', 'logo', 'avatarUrl'])),
    sellerPhone: toText(pick(record, ['sellerPhone', 'seller_phone', 'phone', 'phoneNumber', 'whatsapp'])),
    name: toText(pick(record, ['name', 'title'])) ?? 'Untitled product',
    description: toText(pick(record, ['description', 'details', 'summary'])),
    price: toNumber(pick(record, ['price', 'amount', 'unitPrice'])),
    salePrice: toNumber(pick(record, ['salePrice', 'discountedPrice', 'discountPrice'])),
    stock: toNumber(pick(record, ['stock', 'quantity', 'inventory', 'stockCount'])),
    sku: toText(pick(record, ['sku', 'code', 'reference'])) ?? undefined,
    // Handover hub shown to buyers. Null when the backend sent none â€” the UI
    // then renders the platform default (DEFAULT_DELIVERY_LOCATION) rather than
    // inventing a seller-specific address.
    deliveryLocation: toText(pick(record, ['deliveryLocation', 'delivery_location', 'deliveryHub'])),
    category: normalizeCategory(pick(record, ['category', 'categoryName', 'productCategory'])) ,
    status,
    imageUrl: cover,
    imageAlt: toText(pick(record, ['imageAlt', 'imageDescription', 'alt'])),
    images: gallery.length > 0 ? gallery : null,
    variants: normalizeVariants(pick(record, ['variants', 'options'])),
    condition: normalizeCondition(pick(record, ['condition', 'productCondition', 'product_condition', 'itemCondition', 'item_condition'])),
    featuredInMarketplace: toBoolean(pick(record, ['featuredInMarketplace', 'isFeatured', 'featured'])) === true,
    rating: toNumber(pick(record, ['rating', 'averageRating', 'ratingAverage'])),
    reviews: toNumber(pick(record, ['reviews', 'reviewCount', 'reviewsCount'])),
    createdAt,
    updatedAt: toText(pick(record, ['updatedAt', 'updated', 'modifiedAt'])) ?? createdAt,
  };
}

/** Normalize a product list, dropping entries the backend sent without an id. */
export function normalizeProducts(raw: unknown): Product[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
  return raw.map((entry) => normalizeProduct(entry)).filter((product) => Boolean(product.id));
}

/* ------------------------------ Pagination -------------------------------- */

/**
 * Adapt a list response into the `PaginatedResponse` the hooks expect.
 *
 * Accepted shapes (documented in docs/API_CONTRACT.md):
 * - `{ items, total, page, pageSize }` (frontend contract),
 * - `{ count, results }` / `{ count, next, previous, results }` (DRF),
 * - `{ data: [...] }`, `{ products: [...] }` envelopes,
 * - a bare array.
 *
 * When the backend omits `total`, the honest value is the number of items on
 * THIS page â€” callers must not guess a larger total.
 */
export function toPaginatedResponse(
  raw: unknown,
  requested: { page: number; pageSize: number },
): PaginatedResponse<Product> {
  const source = Array.isArray(raw)
    ? raw
    : pick(isRecord(raw) ? raw : {}, ['items', 'results', 'data', 'products', 'records', 'rows']);
  const items = normalizeProducts(source);
  const record = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
  const total = toNumber(pick(record, ['total', 'count', 'totalCount', 'totalItems'])) ?? items.length;
  const page = toNumber(pick(record, ['page', 'currentPage', 'pageNumber'])) ?? requested.page;
  const pageSize = toNumber(pick(record, ['pageSize', 'perPage', 'limit', 'size'])) ?? requested.pageSize;
  return { items, total, page, pageSize };
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\real\auth.api.ts =====

/**
 * Real Auth API â€” implements the AuthApi contract against the real backend.
 *
 * Mirrors MockAuthApi's interface exactly. When VITE_API_MODE=real, the
 * factory in services/auth.ts swaps this in. The UI never knows the difference.
 *
 * STATUS: this adapter implements the DOCUMENTED contract (docs/API_CONTRACT.md
 * -> Auth). It is NOT yet validated against a live backend â€” the backend does
 * not exist yet. Google authentication in particular is only exercised against
 * the mock: the real backend must verify the Google ID token server-side.
 *
 * Responses are normalized (see ../normalize) so a backend that answers with
 * snake_case keys, an envelope, or `{ is_new_user: true }` still signs the
 * user in, and a contract-violating payload surfaces as a normal ApiError
 * instead of a crash or a half-written session.
 */
import type {
  AuthResponse,
  GoogleLoginRequest,
  LoginRequest,
  PasswordResetRequest,
  PasswordResetResponse,
  RefreshTokenResponse,
  RegisterRequest,
  ResetPasswordRequest,
  User,
  VerifyResetCodeRequest,
  VerifyResetCodeResponse,
} from '../types';
import type { AuthApi } from '../services/auth';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { extractTokenPair, httpClient } from './client';
import { sessionStore } from '../session';
import { isRecord, normalizeUser, pick, toBoolean, toNumber, toText, unwrapEnvelope } from '../normalize';

/** Envelopes a backend may wrap a user payload in. */
const USER_ENVELOPE = ['user', 'data', 'account'];

export class RealAuthApi implements AuthApi {
  async register(data: RegisterRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    return this.persist(await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/register', data, true));
  }

  async login(data: LoginRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    return this.persist(await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/login', data, true));
  }

  /**
   * Google sign-in: POST /auth/google with the Google ID token (JWT) obtained
   * from Google Identity Services â€” see src/lib/googleIdentity.ts. The
   * backend verifies the signature against Google's public keys and answers
   * exactly like login/register (existing accounts link, new emails create +
   * onboard). The frontend does NOT verify the token; it only forwards it.
   */
  async googleLogin(data: GoogleLoginRequest): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    return this.persist(await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/google', data, true));
  }

  async logout(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await httpClient.post<void>('/auth/logout');
    } finally {
      // The local session dies even when the server call fails â€” the tokens
      // must never outlive an explicit sign-out.
      sessionStore.clear();
    }
  }

  async getCurrentUser(): Promise<User> {
    const raw = await httpClient.get<unknown>('/auth/me');
    return normalizeUser(unwrapEnvelope(isRecord(raw) ? raw : {}, USER_ENVELOPE));
  }

  async refreshToken(refreshToken: string): Promise<RefreshTokenResponse> {
    const raw = await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/refresh', { refresh: refreshToken });
    const tokens = extractTokenPair(raw, refreshToken);
    if (!tokens) {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'The authentication server did not return a session. Please try again.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      });
    }
    sessionStore.setTokens(tokens);
    const expiresIn = readExpiresIn(raw);
    return expiresIn === null ? tokens : { ...tokens, expiresIn };
  }

  /**
   * Request password reset â€” POST /auth/forgot-password with email.
   *
   * The backend generates an OTP, stores it securely with expiration, and
   * emails it to the user. The frontend NEVER sees the OTP in production;
   * mock mode returns it in devOtp for testing only.
   *
   * Generic success response prevents email enumeration: same response whether
   * the email exists or not.
   */
  async requestPasswordReset(data: PasswordResetRequest): Promise<PasswordResetResponse> {
    const raw = await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/forgot-password', data, true);
    const body = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
    return {
      message: toText(body.message) ?? 'If an account exists with this email, a verification code has been sent.',
      devOtp: toText(body.devOtp),
    };
  }

  /**
   * Verify password reset OTP â€” POST /auth/verify-reset-code with email and code.
   *
   * The backend validates the OTP is correct, not expired, and under the
   * rate-limit threshold. Returns verified: true on success.
   */
  async verifyResetCode(data: VerifyResetCodeRequest): Promise<VerifyResetCodeResponse> {
    const raw = await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/verify-reset-code', data, true);
    const body = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
    return {
      message: toText(body.message) ?? 'Verification code confirmed.',
      verified: toBoolean(body.verified) ?? true,
    };
  }

  /**
   * Complete password reset â€” POST /auth/reset-password with email, code, and new password.
   *
   * The backend validates the OTP is still valid, enforces password strength,
   * updates the password hash, consumes the OTP (single-use), and revokes all
   * existing sessions for security.
   */
  async resetPassword(data: ResetPasswordRequest): Promise<{ message: string }> {
    const raw = await httpClient.post<unknown>('/auth/reset-password', data, true);
    const body = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
    return {
      message: toText(body.message) ?? 'Password reset successfully. You can now log in with your new password.',
    };
  }

  /**
   * Validate + normalize an auth payload, then persist the session.
   *
   * A payload without a usable token pair fails loudly (the login forms show
   * the message) rather than writing `undefined` into storage.
   */
  private async persist(raw: unknown): Promise<AuthResponse> {
    const body = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
    const tokens = extractTokenPair(body);
    if (!tokens) {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'The authentication server did not return a session. Please try again.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      });
    }
    sessionStore.setTokens(tokens);

    // SimpleJWT token views return only access/refresh. Custom Django auth
    // views may embed the user, so avoid an extra request when they do.
    let user = normalizeUser(unwrapEnvelope(body, USER_ENVELOPE));
    if (!user.id) user = await this.getCurrentUser();
    if (!user.id) {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'Unexpected response from the authentication server.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      });
    }

    const response: AuthResponse = { user, tokens };
    const isNew = pick(body, ['isNewUser', 'isNew']);
    if (isNew !== undefined) response.isNewUser = toBoolean(isNew) === true;
    return response;
  }
}

/** Optional `expiresIn` (seconds) from `{ tokens: {...} }` or a flat body. */
function readExpiresIn(raw: unknown): number | null {
  if (!isRecord(raw)) return null;
  const source = isRecord(raw.tokens) ? raw.tokens : raw;
  return toNumber(pick(source, ['expiresIn', 'expires_in']));
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\api\real\client.ts =====

/** Django REST Framework transport used by every real API service. */
import { apiConfig } from '../config';
import { ApiError, type ApiErrorCode } from '../errors';
import { logApi } from '../logger';
import { sessionStore } from '../session';
import { camelizeDeep, camelizeKey, isRecord, toText } from '../normalize';

function snakeizeKey(key: string): string {
  return key.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (letter) => `_${letter.toLowerCase()}`);
}

function snakeizeDeep(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(snakeizeDeep);
  if (!isRecord(value)) return value;
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, entry]) => [snakeizeKey(key), snakeizeDeep(entry)]));
}

export interface HttpClientOptions {
  method: string;
  path: string;
  body?: unknown;
  /** Skip the default JSON/auth headers (e.g. for FormData). */
  rawBody?: boolean;
  /** Bypass auth header for public endpoints. */
  skipAuth?: boolean;
}

/** Endpoints whose own 401s must NOT trigger a refresh attempt. */
const AUTH_ENDPOINTS = ['/auth/login', '/auth/register', '/auth/google', '/auth/refresh'];

/**
 * Single-flight refresh: concurrent 401s share one refresh request so parallel
 * queries never rotate the refresh token against each other.
 */
let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;

/**
 * Extract the rotated token pair from a refresh response, accepting the
 * documented token aliases plus the standard SimpleJWT `access`/`refresh`
 * names. A refresh response may omit a rotated refresh token, in which case
 * the existing one is retained.
 */
export function extractTokenPair(
  raw: unknown,
  fallbackRefreshToken?: string | null,
): { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string } | null {
  if (!isRecord(raw)) return null;
  const source = isRecord(raw.tokens) ? raw.tokens : raw;
  const accessToken = toText(source.accessToken)
    ?? toText(source.access_token)
    ?? toText(source.access)
    ?? toText(source.token);
  const refreshToken = toText(source.refreshToken)
    ?? toText(source.refresh_token)
    ?? toText(source.refresh)
    ?? toText(fallbackRefreshToken);
  if (!accessToken || !refreshToken) return null;
  return { accessToken, refreshToken };
}

async function tryRefreshOnce(baseUrl: string): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!refreshInFlight) {
    refreshInFlight = (async () => {
      const refreshToken = sessionStore.getRefreshToken();
      if (!refreshToken) return false;
      try {
        const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/auth/refresh`, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ refresh: refreshToken, refreshToken }),
        });
        if (!res.ok) return false;
        const data: unknown = await res.json().catch(() => null);
        const tokens = extractTokenPair(data, refreshToken);
        if (!tokens) return false;
        sessionStore.setTokens(tokens);
        return true;
      } catch {
        return false;
      } finally {
        // Reset after the microtask queue drains so retries work later.
        setTimeout(() => {
          refreshInFlight = null;
        }, 0);
      }
    })();
  }
  return refreshInFlight;
}


/* --------------------------- Error normalization -------------------------- */

/** First human-readable string inside a value that may be nested/arrayed. */
function firstMessage(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value.trim() || undefined;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    for (const entry of value) {
      const text = firstMessage(entry);
      if (text) return text;
    }
    return undefined;
  }
  if (isRecord(value)) {
    return firstMessage(value.message) ?? firstMessage(value.detail) ?? firstMessage(value.error);
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Build `fieldErrors` from the contract shape (`{ fieldErrors: {...} }`) or
 * from Django REST Framework's `{ field: ["message"] }` body, so the forms
 * (which render `error.fieldErrors`) highlight the right inputs either way.
 * Non-field errors are exposed as `_form`, which SignupForm already looks for.
 *
 * Keys are camelized so DRF's `non_field_errors` lands on the same keys the
 * frontend types use.
 */
function collectFieldErrors(data: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, string> | undefined {
  const reserved = new Set(['message', 'detail', 'code', 'errorCode', 'errors', 'fieldErrors', 'nonFieldErrors']);
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};

  const explicit = data.fieldErrors ?? data.errors;
  if (isRecord(explicit)) {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(explicit)) {
      const text = firstMessage(value);
      if (text) out[camelizeKey(key)] = text;
    }
  }

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(data)) {
    if (reserved.has(key)) continue;
    if (!isRecord(value) && !Array.isArray(value)) continue;
    const text = firstMessage(value);
    if (text) out[camelizeKey(key)] = text;
  }

  const nonField = firstMessage(data.nonFieldErrors);
  if (nonField) out._form = nonField;

  return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : undefined;
}

/**
 * Accept only codes the UI understands; otherwise derive one from the HTTP
 * status. A code outside the contract's list is never adopted â€” the frontend
 * must not act on a code it does not define.
 */
function normalizeCode(
  value: unknown,
  status: number,
  fieldErrors?: Record<string, string>,
): ApiErrorCode {
  const raw = toText(value);
  if (raw && (KNOWN_ERROR_CODES as readonly string[]).includes(raw)) return raw as ApiErrorCode;
  // 409 on an email field is the contract's EMAIL_TAKEN (see API_CONTRACT.md).
  if (status === 409 && fieldErrors && Object.keys(fieldErrors).some((key) => /email/i.test(key))) {
    return 'EMAIL_TAKEN';
  }
  return codeFromStatus(status);
}

/** Every code in the ApiErrorCode union â€” used to validate backend responses. */
const KNOWN_ERROR_CODES: ApiErrorCode[] = [
  'VALIDATION_ERROR',
  'EMAIL_TAKEN',
  'INVALID_CREDENTIALS',
  'INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD',
  'WEAK_PASSWORD',
  'MARKETPLACE_LIMIT_REACHED',
  'WORKSHOP_LIMIT_REACHED',
  'RATE_LIMITED',
  'UNAUTHORIZED',
  'FORBIDDEN',
  'NOT_FOUND',
  'CONFLICT',
  'SERVER_ERROR',
  'NETWORK_ERROR',
  'TIMEOUT',
  'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
];

/**
 * Fallback status -> code mapping used when the backend sends no recognizable
 * `code`. Deliberately conservative: statuses we cannot classify become
 * UNKNOWN_ERROR instead of a misleading specific code.
 */
export function codeFromStatus(status: number): ApiErrorCode {
  switch (status) {
    // Backends that answer 400 for validation (instead of 422) must still
    // surface per-field messages in the forms.
    case 400: return 'VALIDATION_ERROR';
    case 401: return 'UNAUTHORIZED';
    case 403: return 'FORBIDDEN';
    case 404: return 'NOT_FOUND';
    case 409: return 'CONFLICT';
    case 408: return 'TIMEOUT';
    case 422: return 'VALIDATION_ERROR';
    case 429: return 'RATE_LIMITED';
    default: return status >= 500 ? 'SERVER_ERROR' : 'UNKNOWN_ERROR';
  }
}

async function parseError(res: Response): Promise<ApiError> {
  let rawBody: unknown;
  try {
    rawBody = await res.json();
  } catch {
    /* non-JSON error body â€” fall through to the status-based error */
  }

  if (isRecord(rawBody)) {
    // Camelize once so `field_errors`, `non_field_errors` and `error_code`
    // style backends land on the same keys the contract uses.
    const data = camelizeDeep<Record<string, unknown>>(rawBody);
    const fieldErrors = collectFieldErrors(data);
    const message =
      firstMessage(data.message)
      ?? firstMessage(data.detail)
      ?? firstMessage(data.error)
      ?? (fieldErrors ? Object.values(fieldErrors)[0] : undefined)
      ?? `Request failed (${res.status}).`;
    return new ApiError({
      message,
      status: res.status,
      code: normalizeCode(data.code ?? data.errorCode, res.status, fieldErrors),
      backendCode: toText(data.code ?? data.errorCode) ?? undefined,
      fieldErrors,
    });
  }

  return new ApiError({
    message: `Request failed (${res.status}).`,
    status: res.status,
    code: codeFromStatus(res.status),
  });
}

export class HttpClient {
  private readonly baseUrl: string;

  constructor() {
    this.baseUrl = apiConfig.baseUrl;
  }

  async request<T>(options: HttpClientOptions): Promise<T> {
    const { method, path, body, rawBody, skipAuth } = options;
    logApi(method, path);

    const buildInit = (): RequestInit => {
      const headers: Record<string, string> = { Accept: 'application/json' };
      if (!rawBody) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
      const csrfToken = readCookie('csrftoken');
      if (csrfToken && method !== 'GET' && method !== 'HEAD' && method !== 'OPTIONS') {
        headers['X-CSRFToken'] = csrfToken;
      }
      if (!skipAuth) {
        const token = sessionStore.getAccessToken();
        if (token) headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`;
      }
      const init: RequestInit = { method, headers, credentials: 'include' };
      if (body !== undefined) {
        init.body = rawBody ? (body as BodyInit) : JSON.stringify(snakeizeDeep(body));
      }
      return init;
    };

    let res: Response;
    try {
      res = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${path}`, buildInit());
    } catch {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'Network error. Please check your connection.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'NETWORK_ERROR',
      });
    }

    // SECURITY: on 401, try ONE silent refresh (single-flight) and retry the
    // original request with the rotated access token. Auth endpoints exclude
    // themselves so a failed login can never cascade into a refresh loop.
    if (res.status === 401 && !skipAuth && !AUTH_ENDPOINTS.some((p) => path.startsWith(p))) {
      const refreshed = await tryRefreshOnce(this.baseUrl);
      if (refreshed) {
        try {
          res = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${path}`, buildInit());
        } catch {
          throw new ApiError({ message: 'Network error. Please check your connection.', status: 0, code: 'NETWORK_ERROR' });
        }
      } else {
        // Refresh failed â€” the session is truly dead; drop stale tokens.
        sessionStore.clear();
      }
    }

    if (!res.ok) {
      throw await parseError(res);
    }

    if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T;

    try {
      // Key normalization happens ONCE here, so every Real*Api implementation
      // receives the camelCase contract shape even when the backend answers
      // with `featured_in_marketplace`, `sale_price` or `created_at` keys.
      return camelizeDeep<T>(await res.json());
    } catch {
      return undefined as T;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Multipart/form-data upload. SEPARATE from the JSON request family on
   * purpose: uploads carry FormData (no Content-Type header â€” the browser
   * sets the multipart boundary) and their success is defined ONLY by the
   * backend response parsed here. A local preview rendering is never proof
   * that an upload succeeded.
   */
  async upload<T>(path: string, formData: FormData): Promise<T> {
    logApi('POST', path);
    const buildInit = (): RequestInit => {
      const headers: Record<string, string> = { Accept: 'application/json' };
      const token = sessionStore.getAccessToken();
      if (token) headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`;
      const csrfToken = readCookie('csrftoken');
      if (csrfToken) headers['X-CSRFToken'] = csrfToken;
      return { method: 'POST', headers, body: formData, credentials: 'include' };
    };

    let res: Response;
    try {
      res = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${path}`, buildInit());
    } catch {
      throw new ApiError({ message: 'Network error. Please check your connection.', status: 0, code: 'NETWORK_ERROR' });
    }

    if (res.status === 401 && sessionStore.getAccessToken()) {
      const refreshed = await tryRefreshOnce(this.baseUrl);
      if (refreshed) {
        try {
          res = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${path}`, buildInit());
        } catch {
          throw new ApiError({ message: 'Network error. Please check your connection.', status: 0, code: 'NETWORK_ERROR' });
        }
      } else {
        sessionStore.clear();
      }
    }

    if (!res.ok) throw await parseError(res);
    if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T;
    try {
      return camelizeDeep<T>(await res.json());
    } catch {
      return undefined as T;
    }
  }

  get<T>(path: string, skipAuth = false): Promise<T> {
    return this.request<T>({ method: 'GET', path, skipAuth });
  }

  post<T>(path: string, body?: unknown, skipAuth = false): Promise<T> {
    return this.request<T>({ method: 'POST', path, body, skipAuth });
  }

  patch<T>(path: string, body?: unknown, skipAuth = false): Promise<T> {
    return this.request<T>({ method: 'PATCH', path, body, skipAuth });
  }

  delete<T>(path: string, body?: unknown, skipAuth = false): Promise<T> {
    return this.request<T>({ method: 'DELETE', path, body, skipAuth });
  }
}

/** Shared instance â€” use this unless you need a custom-configured client. */
export const httpClient = new HttpClient();

function readCookie(name: string): string | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  const prefix = `${name}=`;
  const match = document.cookie.split('; ').find((entry) => entry.startsWith(prefix));
  return match ? decodeURIComponent(match.slice(prefix.length)) : null;
}

/**
 * Real Orders API â€” implements the OrdersApi contract against the real
 * backend (docs/API_CONTRACT.md -> Orders).
 *
 * The adapter ONLY relays what the backend reports: an order exists when the
 * backend created it, its status is whatever the backend returns, and its
 * amount is whatever the backend computed. Nothing is simulated locally.
 */
import type { CreateOrderRequest, Order, OrderItem, OrderQueryParams, PaginatedResponse } from '../types';
import type { OrdersApi } from '../services/orders';
import { ApiError } from '../errors';
import { httpClient } from './client';
import { isRecord, toNumber, toText, unwrapEnvelope } from '../normalize';

/** Envelopes a backend may wrap an order payload in. */
const ORDER_ENVELOPE = ['order', 'data', 'result'];

const VALID_ORDER_STATUSES = ['processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'];

/**
 * Normalize one order line item. Malformed entries (no productId) are dropped
 * rather than guessed â€” analytics must never count a line the backend did not
 * actually report.
 */
export function normalizeOrderItem(raw: unknown): OrderItem | null {
  const record = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
  const productId = toText(record.productId) ?? toText(record.product) ?? null;
  if (!productId) return null;
  const quantity = Math.max(1, Math.round(toNumber(record.quantity) ?? 1));
  const unitPrice = toNumber(record.unitPrice) ?? toNumber(record.price);
  const lineTotal = toNumber(record.lineTotal) ?? toNumber(record.total);
  return {
    productId,
    productName: toText(record.productName) ?? toText(record.name) ?? '',
    quantity,
    unitPrice,
    // Fall back to the documented arithmetic only when the backend omitted
    // lineTotal but did send a unit price â€” never a fabricated amount.
    lineTotal: lineTotal ?? (unitPrice != null ? unitPrice * quantity : null),
    sellerId: toText(record.sellerId) ?? null,
  };
}

/**
 * Normalize one order payload into the UI's `Order` shape.
 *
 * `status` is the backend's word only: an unrecognized status throws instead
 * of being silently mapped to a plausible one.
 */
export function normalizeOrder(raw: unknown): Order {
  const record = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
  const status = toText(record.status) ?? toText(record.state);
  if (!status || !VALID_ORDER_STATUSES.includes(status)) {
    throw new ApiError({
      message: 'The server returned an order with an unknown status.',
      status: 0,
      code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
    });
  }
  const createdAt = toText(record.createdAt) ?? toText(record.created) ?? '';
  // Line items: REQUIRED on /seller/orders (analytics depends on them),
  // optional elsewhere. When absent the field stays undefined and the UI
  // falls back to the order total â€” nothing is invented here.
  const items = Array.isArray(record.items)
    ? record.items
        .map((entry) => normalizeOrderItem(entry))
        .filter((entry): entry is OrderItem => entry !== null)
    : undefined;
  return {
    id: toText(record.id) ?? toText(record.uuid) ?? '',
    reference: toText(record.reference) ?? toText(record.orderReference) ?? '',
    buyerName: toText(record.buyerName) ?? toText(record.customerName) ?? '',
    buyerInitials: toText(record.buyerInitials) ?? undefined,
    amount: toNumber(record.amount) ?? toNumber(record.total),
    status: status as Order['status'],
    createdAt,
    ...(items ? { items } : {}),
  };
}

/** Query string shared by both order-list endpoints. */
function buildOrderQuery(page: number, pageSize: number, params: OrderQueryParams): string {
  const sp = new URLSearchParams();
  sp.set('page', String(page));
  sp.set('page_size', String(pageSize));
  // Optional ISO window â€” server-side period filtering (docs/API_CONTRACT.md).
  if (params.since) sp.set('since', params.since);
  if (params.until) sp.set('until', params.until);
  return sp.toString();
}

/**
 * Parse either documented list envelope. Accepts a bare array, `{ items }`,
 * `{ results }` (DRF), `{ data }` or `{ orders }`.
 */
function toOrderPage(raw: unknown, page: number, pageSize: number): PaginatedResponse<Order> {
  const items: unknown[] = Array.isArray(raw)
    ? raw
    : isRecord(raw) && Array.isArray(raw.items) ? raw.items
    : isRecord(raw) && Array.isArray(raw.results) ? raw.results
    : isRecord(raw) && Array.isArray(raw.data) ? raw.data
    : isRecord(raw) && Array.isArray(raw.orders) ? raw.orders
    : [];
  const record = isRecord(raw) ? raw : {};
  const total = toNumber(record.total) ?? toNumber(record.count) ?? items.length;
  return {
    items: items.map((entry) => normalizeOrder(entry)),
    page,
    pageSize,
    total: Math.max(total, items.length),
  };
}

export class RealOrdersApi implements OrdersApi {
  async getOrders(params: OrderQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Order>> {
    const page = Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1);
    const pageSize = Math.max(1, params.pageSize ?? 20);
    const raw = await httpClient.get<unknown>(`/orders?${buildOrderQuery(page, pageSize, params)}`);
    return toOrderPage(raw, page, pageSize);
  }

  /**
   * Orders visible to the signed-in SELLER â€” every order containing at least
   * one line of a product they own, newest first, WITH line items. Sales
   * Analytics derives every figure from this endpoint; the adapter relays
   * exactly what the backend computed and invents nothing
   * (docs/API_CONTRACT.md -> Orders).
   */
  async getSellerOrders(params: OrderQueryParams = {}): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Order>> {
    const page = Math.max(1, params.page ?? 1);
    const pageSize = Math.max(1, params.pageSize ?? 20);
    const raw = await httpClient.get<unknown>(`/seller/orders?${buildOrderQuery(page, pageSize, params)}`);
    return toOrderPage(raw, page, pageSize);
  }

  async getOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> {
    const raw = await httpClient.get<unknown>(`/orders/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`);
    const order = normalizeOrder(unwrapEnvelope(raw, ORDER_ENVELOPE));
    if (!order.id) {
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'The server returned an unexpected order response.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      });
    }
    return order;
  }

  async createOrder(data: CreateOrderRequest): Promise<Order> {
    const raw = await httpClient.post<unknown>('/orders', data);
    const order = normalizeOrder(unwrapEnvelope(isRecord(raw) ? raw : {}, ORDER_ENVELOPE));
    if (!order.id) {
      // The backend MUST return the created order. The frontend never
      // pretends an order was created without the backend saying so.
      throw new ApiError({
        message: 'The server did not confirm the order. Check your order history before retrying.',
        status: 0,
        code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      });
    }
    return order;
  }
}
