import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { Link, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import Button from './ui/Button';
import ArrowIcon from './ui/ArrowIcon';
import { prefetchPropsForPath, triggerHomeSectionsLoad } from '../lib/prefetch';

const Navbar = ({ cartCount }) => {
  const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);
  const [menuOpen, setMenuOpen] = useState(false);
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleScroll = () => {
      setScrolled(window.scrollY > 40);
    };
    window.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll);
    return () => window.removeEventListener("scroll", handleScroll);
  }, []);

  const toggleMenu = () => setMenuOpen(!menuOpen);

  const handleAuthClick = (mode) => {
    navigate(`/auth/${mode}`);
    setMenuOpen(false);
  };

  /**
   * In-page section links (#marketplace, #dashboard, ...). Those sections only
   * exist after the below-the-fold chunk loads, so we trigger that load and
   * smooth-scroll once the target node appears.
   */
  const handleSectionClick = (selector) => (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    triggerHomeSectionsLoad();
    const tryScroll = () => {
      const el = document.querySelector(selector);
      if (el) el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
      else window.setTimeout(tryScroll, 120);
    };
    window.setTimeout(tryScroll, 50);
    setMenuOpen(false);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <nav className={`navbar ${scrolled ? "scrolled" : ""}`}>
        <div className="container">
          <Link to="/" className="logo" {...prefetchPropsForPath('/')}>
            <img src="/logo.png" alt="Universe" className="logo-img" />
          </Link>

          <ul className="nav-menu">
            <li><Link to="/" className="nav-link active" {...prefetchPropsForPath('/')}>Home</Link></li>
            <li><Link to="#marketplace" className="nav-link" onClick={handleSectionClick('#marketplace')}>Marketplace</Link></li>
            <li><Link to="#features-showcase" className="nav-link" onClick={handleSectionClick('#features-showcase')}>Features</Link></li>
            <li><Link to="#dashboard" className="nav-link" onClick={handleSectionClick('#dashboard')}>Dashboard</Link></li>
            <li><Link to="#contact" className="nav-link" onClick={handleSectionClick('#contact')}>Contact</Link></li>
          </ul>

          <div className="nav-actions">
            <button className="cart-btn" aria-label="Shopping Cart">
              <svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
                <path d="M6 2L3 6v14a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h14a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V6l-3-4z"></path>
                <line x1="3" y1="6" x2="21" y2="6"></line>
                <path d="M16 10a4 4 0 0 1-8 0"></path>
              </svg>
              {cartCount > 0 && <span className="cart-count">{cartCount}</span>}
            </button>
            <Button className="btn-outline" onClick={() => handleAuthClick('login')} {...prefetchPropsForPath('/auth')}>Sign In</Button>
            <Button className="btn-primary" onClick={() => handleAuthClick('signup')} {...prefetchPropsForPath('/auth/signup')}>Get Started <ArrowIcon /></Button>
          </div>

          <button className={`hamburger ${menuOpen ? "open" : ""}`} onClick={toggleMenu} aria-label="Toggle Menu">
            <span></span>
            <span></span>
            <span></span>
          </button>
        </div>
      </nav>

      {/* Mobile Drawer Menu */}
      <div className={`mobile-menu-overlay ${menuOpen ? "open" : ""}`} onClick={toggleMenu}></div>
      <div className={`mobile-menu ${menuOpen ? "open" : ""}`}>
        <ul className="mobile-nav">
          <li><Link to="/" className="mobile-nav-link" onClick={toggleMenu} {...prefetchPropsForPath('/')}>Home</Link></li>
          <li><Link to="#marketplace" className="mobile-nav-link" onClick={handleSectionClick('#marketplace')}>Marketplace</Link></li>

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\hooks\useAuth.ts =====

/**
 * Auth hooks â€” consume the authApi service so components never know whether
 * data comes from mock or real backend. Handles login, register, logout, and
 * current-user fetching with TanStack Query.
 *
 * Security behaviors:
 * - useCurrentUser() silently refreshes ONE time on a 401 before giving up,
 *   so an expired access token never logs the user out mid-session while a
 *   valid refresh token exists.
 * - useLogin/useRegister wipe the whole query cache on success so data that
 *   belonged to a PREVIOUS account can never leak into the new session
 *   (shared-computer safety).
 * - Login/register return the user to the page they originally wanted
 *   (location.state.from) instead of a hard-coded landing page.
 */
import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { useLocation, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { authApi } from '../api/services/auth';
import { ApiError, isAuthError } from '../api/errors';
import { sessionStore } from '../api/session';
import type {
  GoogleLoginRequest,
  LoginRequest,
  PasswordResetRequest,
  PasswordResetResponse,
  RegisterRequest,
  ResetPasswordRequest,
  User,
  VerifyResetCodeRequest,
  VerifyResetCodeResponse,
} from '../api/types';

const CURRENT_USER_KEY = ['currentUser'];
const BUYER_LANDING_PATH = '/marketplace';

/** Fetch the currently authenticated user (skipped when no token exists). */
export function useCurrentUser() {
  return useQuery<User, ApiError>({
    queryKey: CURRENT_USER_KEY,
    queryFn: async () => {
      try {
        return await authApi.getCurrentUser();
      } catch (error) {
        // Access token expired â€” attempt exactly one silent refresh, then retry.
        if (isAuthError(error) && sessionStore.getRefreshToken()) {
          try {
            await authApi.refreshToken(sessionStore.getRefreshToken()!);
            return await authApi.getCurrentUser();
          } catch {
            // Refresh failed â€” clear stale tokens so guards redirect to login.
            sessionStore.clear();
            throw error;
          }
        }
        throw error;
      }
    },
    enabled: sessionStore.hasTokens(),
    retry: false,
    staleTime: 60 * 1000,
  });
}

/** Login mutation â€” on success, caches the user and honors the return URL. */
export function useLogin() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const location = useLocation();
  const from = (location.state as { from?: { pathname?: string } } | null)?.from;

  return useMutation<User, ApiError, LoginRequest>({
    mutationFn: async (data) => {
      const res = await authApi.login(data);
      return res.user;
    },
    onSuccess: (user) => {
      // Clear any data cached under the previous account, then seed this one.
      queryClient.clear();
      queryClient.setQueryData(CURRENT_USER_KEY, user);
      const fallback = user.accountType === 'seller' ? '/seller' : BUYER_LANDING_PATH;
      const returnTo = from?.pathname && from.pathname !== '/auth' ? from : null;
      navigate(returnTo ? `${returnTo.pathname}${location.state?.from?.search ?? ''}` : fallback);
    },
  });
}

/** Register mutation â€” on success, stores sessions and redirects. */
export function useRegister() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  return useMutation<User, ApiError, RegisterRequest>({
    mutationFn: async (data) => {
      const res = await authApi.register(data);
      return res.user;
    },
    onSuccess: (user) => {
      queryClient.clear();
      queryClient.setQueryData(CURRENT_USER_KEY, user);
      navigate(user.accountType === 'seller' ? '/seller/onboarding' : BUYER_LANDING_PATH);
    },
  });
}

/**
 * Google sign-in mutation â€” same session/cache flow as useLogin, with two
 * additions:
 * - Guards against contract-violating backend responses (missing user or
 *   tokens) so a broken backend surfaces as a normal auth error, never a
 *   crash.
 * - A brand-new Google user (isNewUser, first sign-in for that email) follows
 *   the register-style redirect â€” sellers go to onboarding â€” while an
 *   existing user follows the login-style one (return URL / dashboard).
 *
 * The credential is the Google ID token (JWT) obtained from the real Google
 * Identity Services button; it is passed opaquely to authApi.googleLogin().
 */
export function useGoogleLogin() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const location = useLocation();
  const from = (location.state as { from?: { pathname?: string } } | null)?.from;

  return useMutation<{ user: User; isNewUser: boolean }, ApiError, GoogleLoginRequest>({
    mutationFn: async (data) => {
      const res = await authApi.googleLogin(data);
      if (!res || typeof res !== 'object' || !res.user?.id || !res.tokens?.accessToken) {
        throw new ApiError({
          message: 'Unexpected response from the authentication server.',
          status: 0,
          code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
        });
      }
      return { user: res.user, isNewUser: Boolean(res.isNewUser) };
    },
    onSuccess: ({ user, isNewUser }) => {
      // Clear any data cached under the previous account, then seed this one.
      queryClient.clear();
      queryClient.setQueryData(CURRENT_USER_KEY, user);
      if (isNewUser) {
        // Fresh Google signup â€” same destination as email registration.
        navigate(user.accountType === 'seller' ? '/seller/onboarding' : BUYER_LANDING_PATH);
        return;
      }
      const fallback = user.accountType === 'seller' ? '/seller' : BUYER_LANDING_PATH;
      const returnTo = from?.pathname && from.pathname !== '/auth' ? from : null;
      navigate(returnTo ? `${returnTo.pathname}${location.state?.from?.search ?? ''}` : fallback);
    },
  });
}

/** Logout mutation â€” clears tokens and resets the query cache. */
export function useLogout() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  return useMutation<void, ApiError, void>({
    mutationFn: () => authApi.logout(),
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.clear();
      navigate('/');
    },
    onError: () => {
      // Even if the server logout fails, clear local state.
      queryClient.clear();
      sessionStore.clear();
      navigate('/');
    },
  });
}

/**
 * Request password reset mutation â€” sends OTP to email.
 *
 * Returns PasswordResetResponse with devOtp in development mode for testing.
 * Generic success response prevents email enumeration.
 */
export function useRequestPasswordReset() {
  return useMutation<PasswordResetResponse, ApiError, PasswordResetRequest>({
    mutationFn: (data) => authApi.requestPasswordReset(data),
  });
}

/**
 * Verify reset code mutation â€” validates the OTP.
 *
 * Returns verified: true on success. Rate limited to prevent brute force.
 */
export function useVerifyResetCode() {

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\hooks\useIntersectionObserver.js =====

import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

export const useIntersectionObserver = (options = {}) => {
  const [isIntersecting, setIsIntersecting] = useState(false);
  const elementRef = useRef(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => {
      setIsIntersecting(entry.isIntersecting);
    }, options);

    if (elementRef.current) {
      observer.observe(elementRef.current);
    }

    return () => {
      if (elementRef.current) {
        observer.unobserve(elementRef.current);
      }
    };
  }, [options]);

  return [elementRef, isIntersecting];
};

/**
 * Product hooks â€” consume the productsApi service with TanStack Query.
 * Components never know whether data comes from mock or real backend.
 */
import { useInfiniteQuery, useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { productsApi } from '../api/services/products';
import { ApiError } from '../api/errors';
import type {
  CreateProductRequest,
  PaginatedResponse,
  Product,
  ProductQueryParams,
  UpdateProductRequest,
} from '../api/types';

const PRODUCTS_KEY = 'products';

function productsQueryKey(params?: ProductQueryParams) {
  return [PRODUCTS_KEY, params ?? {}];
}

/** Fetch a paginated product list, optionally filtered. */
export function useProducts(params?: ProductQueryParams) {
  return useQuery<Product[], ApiError>({
    queryKey: productsQueryKey(params),
    queryFn: async () => {
      const res = await productsApi.getProducts(params);
      return res.items;
    },
    placeholderData: (prev) => prev,
  });
}

/**
 * Paginated variant of `useProducts` for catalogs that can exceed one page
 * (the public marketplace). `fetchNextPage()` appends the next server page on
 * demand, so no product is unreachable just because it sits beyond the first
 * page â€” the backend still owns filtering and paging, one request per page.
 *
 * Data lives under its OWN query key (`['products', 'pages', params]`) because
 * an infinite query caches a different shape than `useProducts()`'s bare
 * array; sharing the key would hand one hook the other's data. Product writes
 * still refresh it: `invalidateQueries(['products'])` matches by key prefix.
 */
export function useInfiniteProducts(params?: ProductQueryParams) {
  const pageSize = params?.pageSize ?? 40;
  // `page` is driven by the infinite query itself, never by the caller.
  const filters = { ...(params ?? {}), page: undefined, pageSize };
  return useInfiniteQuery<PaginatedResponse<Product>, ApiError>({
    queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY, 'pages', filters],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => productsApi.getProducts({ ...params, page: Number(pageParam), pageSize }),
    initialPageParam: 1,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage, allPages) => {
      // A page with no items means the catalog is exhausted (or the backend
      // ignored `page`) â€” stop instead of re-requesting the same rows forever.
      if (lastPage.items.length === 0) return undefined;
      const loaded = allPages.reduce((count, page) => count + page.items.length, 0);
      return loaded < lastPage.total ? lastPage.page + 1 : undefined;
    },
  });
}

/** Fetch a single product by id. */
export function useProduct(id: string) {
  return useQuery<Product, ApiError>({
    queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY, 'detail', id],
    queryFn: () => productsApi.getProduct(id),
    enabled: Boolean(id),
  });
}

/** Create a product â€” invalidates the product list on success. */
export function useCreateProduct() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation<Product, ApiError, CreateProductRequest>({
    mutationFn: (data) => productsApi.createProduct(data),
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY] });
    },
  });
}

/** Update a product â€” invalidates the list and detail cache on success. */
export function useUpdateProduct() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation<Product, ApiError, { id: string; data: UpdateProductRequest }>({
    mutationFn: ({ id, data }) => productsApi.updateProduct(id, data),
    onSuccess: (_, { id }) => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY] });
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY, 'detail', id] });
    },
  });
}

/** Delete a product â€” invalidates the product list on success. */
export function useDeleteProduct() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation<void, ApiError, string>({
    mutationFn: (id) => productsApi.deleteProduct(id),
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [PRODUCTS_KEY] });
    },
  });
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\hooks\useSellerAnalytics.ts =====

/**
 * Seller sales analytics â€” every figure on the Sales Analytics page is
 * computed here from the seller's REAL orders (GET /seller/orders).
 *
 * There is no mock layer in this file: when there are no orders the page
 * shows its empty state, and when the backend is unreachable it shows the
 * error â€” never invented numbers.
 *
 * Windows: the selected range (7d/30d/90d) is aggregated for the CURRENT
 * period and again for the immediately PREVIOUS period of the same length,
 * which is what the "vs last period" trends compare against. Orders are
 * fetched window-by-window (server-side since/until filtering) and paged
 * through completely so the totals cover every order, not just page 1.
 */
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ordersApi } from '../api/services/orders';
import { ApiError } from '../api/errors';
import type { Order } from '../api/types';
import { useCurrentUser } from './useAuth';

export type SalesRange = '7d' | '30d' | '90d';

/** Length of each range in days. */
const RANGE_DAYS: Record<SalesRange, number> = { '7d': 7, '30d': 30, '90d': 90 };

/** Human label per range, shown in the chart subtitle. */
export const RANGE_LABELS: Record<SalesRange, string> = {
  '7d': 'Last 7 days',
  '30d': 'Last 30 days',
  '90d': 'Last 90 days',
};

/** Page size for the order page walk â€” one page usually covers every order. */
const PAGE_SIZE = 100;
/** Safety cap: 50 pages x 100 orders is far beyond any realistic window. */
const MAX_PAGES = 50;

function startOfDay(date: Date): Date {
  const d = new Date(date);
  d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  return d;
}

function addDays(date: Date, days: number): Date {
  const d = new Date(date);
  d.setDate(d.getDate() + days);
  return d;
}

export interface AnalyticsWindows {
  /** Current period: [since, until]. */
  since: string;
  until: string;
  /** Previous period of the same length, immediately before `since`. */
  prevSince: string;
  prevUntil: string;
}

/** Calendar windows (local time) for a range: current + previous period. */
export function analyticsWindows(range: SalesRange, now = new Date()): AnalyticsWindows {
  const days = RANGE_DAYS[range];
  const since = startOfDay(addDays(now, -(days - 1)));
  const prevSince = startOfDay(addDays(since, -days));
  return {
    since: since.toISOString(),
    until: now.toISOString(),
    prevSince: prevSince.toISOString(),
    prevUntil: since.toISOString(),
  };
}

/** Walk every page of the seller's orders inside a window. */
async function fetchOrdersInRange(since: string, until: string): Promise<Order[]> {
  const all: Order[] = [];
  for (let page = 1; page <= MAX_PAGES; page += 1) {
    const res = await ordersApi.getSellerOrders({ since, until, page, pageSize: PAGE_SIZE });
    all.push(...res.items);
    const loaded = (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE + res.items.length;
    if (res.items.length === 0 || loaded >= res.total) break;
  }
  return all;
}

/** All of the seller's orders inside one window, refreshed about every minute. */
export function useSellerOrders(span: { since: string; until: string }) {
  return useQuery<Order[], ApiError>({
    queryKey: ['seller-orders', span.since, span.until],
    queryFn: () => fetchOrdersInRange(span.since, span.until),
    // Realtime-enough for a dashboard: fresh data on window focus and a
    // background refresh every minute. Same-key refreshes keep the previous
    // rows visible (no flicker back to "loading").
    staleTime: 30_000,
    refetchInterval: 60_000,
    refetchOnWindowFocus: true,
  });
}

/* ----------------------------- Metric math ------------------------------ */

/**
 * Revenue one order contributes to THIS seller: the sum of the seller's own
 * line totals, excluding cancelled orders. Falls back to the backend-computed
 * order total only when the backend omitted line items (optional outside
 * /seller/orders) â€” never a locally recomputed guess.
 */
export function orderSellerAmount(order: Order, sellerId?: string | null): number {
  if (order.status === 'cancelled') return 0;
  if (Array.isArray(order.items) && order.items.length > 0) {
    return order.items.reduce((sum, item) => {
      if (sellerId && item.sellerId && item.sellerId !== sellerId) return sum;
      const line = item.lineTotal ?? (item.unitPrice != null ? item.unitPrice * item.quantity : 0);
      return sum + (Number.isFinite(line) ? line : 0);
    }, 0);
  }
  return order.amount ?? 0;
}

/** Units of THIS seller's products inside one order (cancelled excluded). */
export function orderSellerUnits(order: Order, sellerId?: string | null): number {
  if (order.status === 'cancelled') return 0;
  if (!Array.isArray(order.items)) return 0;
  return order.items.reduce((sum, item) => {
    if (sellerId && item.sellerId && item.sellerId !== sellerId) return sum;
    return sum + item.quantity;
  }, 0);
}

/** One revenue bucket for the chart. */
export interface RevenueBucket {
  /** Short axis label ("Mon", "12", "25"). */
  label: string;
  /** Full label for tooltips ("Mon, Sep 15"). */
  fullLabel: string;
  /** Seller revenue inside the bucket. */
  value: number;
  /** Bar height as a percentage of the tallest bucket. */
  height: number;
}

export interface SellerSalesSummary {
  /** Revenue from non-cancelled orders in the window. */
  revenue: number;
  /** Every order placed in the window (any status). */
  orders: number;
  /** Units sold from non-cancelled orders. */
  productsSold: number;
  /** Cancelled orders in the window (the contract's refund stand-in). */
  refunds: number;
  /** Newest-first orders (the view caps how many it displays). */
  recent: Order[];
  /** Revenue chart buckets, oldest â†’ newest. */
  series: RevenueBucket[];
  /** How many orders the figures are based on (shown under the chart). */
  basis: number;
}

/** Build the chart buckets for a range and drop the orders into them. */
function buildSeries(
  orders: Order[],
  range: SalesRange,
  sellerId: string | null,
  now: Date,
): RevenueBucket[] {
  const windows: { start: Date; end: Date; label: string; fullLabel: string }[] = [];

  if (range === '90d') {
    // 13 rolling 7-day buckets ending today â€” months are too coarse for a
    // 90-day window and daily bars far too dense.
    const buckets = 13;
    for (let i = 0; i < buckets; i += 1) {
      const start = startOfDay(addDays(now, -((buckets - i) * 7 - 1)));
      const end = i === buckets - 1 ? now : startOfDay(addDays(now, -((buckets - i - 1) * 7 - 1)));
      windows.push({
        start,
        end,
        label: String(start.getDate()),
        fullLabel: start.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { day: 'numeric', month: 'short' }),
      });
    }
  } else {
    const days = RANGE_DAYS[range];
    for (let i = 0; i < days; i += 1) {
      const start = startOfDay(addDays(now, -(days - 1 - i)));
      const end = i === days - 1 ? now : startOfDay(addDays(start, 1));
      windows.push({
        start,
        end,
        label: range === '7d'
          ? start.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: 'short' })
          : String(start.getDate()),
        fullLabel: start.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: 'short', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' }),
      });
    }
  }

  const sums = windows.map(() => 0);
  for (const order of orders) {
    const created = new Date(order.createdAt).getTime();
    if (Number.isNaN(created)) continue;
    const bucket = windows.findIndex((w) => created >= w.start.getTime() && created < w.end.getTime());
    if (bucket !== -1) sums[bucket] += orderSellerAmount(order, sellerId);
  }

  const max = sums.reduce((m, value) => Math.max(m, value), 0);
  return windows.map((w, index) => ({
    label: w.label,
    fullLabel: w.fullLabel,
    value: sums[index],
    height: max > 0 ? Math.max(2, Math.round((sums[index] / max) * 100)) : 0,
  }));
}

/** Compute the whole summary for one window from its orders. */
export function computeSellerSales(
  orders: Order[],
  options: { range: SalesRange; sellerId?: string | null; now?: Date },
): SellerSalesSummary {
  const now = options.now ?? new Date();
  const sellerId = options.sellerId ?? null;
  const sorted = [...orders].sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt));
  return {
    revenue: sorted.reduce((sum, order) => sum + orderSellerAmount(order, sellerId), 0),
    orders: sorted.length,
    productsSold: sorted.reduce((sum, order) => sum + orderSellerUnits(order, sellerId), 0),
    refunds: sorted.filter((order) => order.status === 'cancelled').length,
    recent: sorted.slice(0, 5),
    series: buildSeries(sorted, options.range, sellerId, now),
    basis: sorted.length,
  };
}

/** Percentage change vs the previous period; null when there is no baseline. */
export function trendPercent(current: number, previous: number): number | null {
  if (!Number.isFinite(previous) || previous <= 0) return null;
  return ((current - previous) / previous) * 100;
}

export interface SellerSales {
  /** Current-window summary (zeros while loading). */
  summary: SellerSalesSummary;
  /** Previous-window summary for the trends; null until it has loaded. */
  previous: SellerSalesSummary | null;
  /** True until BOTH windows have loaded at least once. */
  isLoading: boolean;
  /** True while a refresh (background or manual) is in flight. */
  isFetching: boolean;
  isError: boolean;
  error: ApiError | null;
  refetch: () => void;
  /** True when the current window genuinely has no orders. */
  isEmpty: boolean;
}

/**
 * Everything the Sales Analytics page renders, computed from real orders.
 * Current and previous windows load independently; the previous window only
 * feeds the trends, so a missing previous period degrades to "no previous
 * data" instead of a fake percentage.
 */
export function useSellerSales(range: SalesRange): SellerSales {
  const { data: user } = useCurrentUser();
  const sellerId = user?.id ?? null;
  const windows = useMemo(() => analyticsWindows(range), [range]);

  const currentQuery = useSellerOrders({ since: windows.since, until: windows.until });
  const previousQuery = useSellerOrders({ since: windows.prevSince, until: windows.prevUntil });

  const summary = useMemo(
    () => computeSellerSales(currentQuery.data ?? [], { range, sellerId }),
    [currentQuery.data, range, sellerId],
  );
  const previous = useMemo(
    () => (previousQuery.data ? computeSellerSales(previousQuery.data, { range, sellerId }) : null),
    [previousQuery.data, range, sellerId],
  );

  const isError = currentQuery.isError;
  const error = currentQuery.error ?? null;

  return {
    summary,
    previous,
    isLoading: currentQuery.isLoading || previousQuery.isLoading,
    isFetching: currentQuery.isFetching || previousQuery.isFetching,
    isError,
    error,
    refetch: () => {
      void currentQuery.refetch();
      void previousQuery.refetch();
    },
    isEmpty: !currentQuery.isLoading && !isError && summary.orders === 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Storefront hooks â€” consume the storefrontApi service with TanStack Query.
 * The storefront is public: no session is required to view a store.
 */
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { storefrontApi } from '../api/services/storefront';
import { productsApi } from '../api/services/products';
import { ApiError } from '../api/errors';
import { normalizeStorefrontProduct } from '../api/real/storefront.normalize';
import type { Storefront } from '../api/types';

const STOREFRONT_KEY = 'storefront';

/** Resolve a store's private marketplace by domain slug. */
export function useStorefront(slug?: string) {
  return useQuery<Storefront, ApiError>({
    queryKey: [STOREFRONT_KEY, slug ?? ''],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const store = await storefrontApi.getStorefront(slug ?? '');
      if (store.products.length > 0 || !store.sellerId) return store;

      const catalog = await productsApi.getAllProducts({ sellerId: store.sellerId, pageSize: 50 });
      const products = catalog.items
        .map((product) => normalizeStorefrontProduct(product))
        .filter((product) => product !== null);
      const counts = products.reduce((result, product) => {
        result.all += 1;
        result[product.category] += 1;
        return result;
      }, { ...store.catalogCounts, all: 0 });
      return { ...store, products, catalogCounts: counts };
    },
    enabled: Boolean(slug),
    staleTime: 60 * 1000,
  });
}

import { useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

  ChangePasswordRequest,

  UpdateSellerProfileRequest,
  UpdateUserRequest,
  User,
} from '../api/types';

/** Fetch the current user's seller profile. */

 * button on a product page. Stays disabled until the id is resolved, so the

export function usePublicSellerProfile(sellerId?: string | null) {

    queryFn: () => usersApi.getPublicSellerProfile(sellerId as string),

  return useMutation<SellerProfile, ApiError, UpdateSellerProfileRequest>({
    mutationFn: (data) => usersApi.updateSellerProfile(data),
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: SELLER_PROFILE_KEY });
      // The public storefront derives from the profile (template, pickup hub,
      // support email, logo...) â€” bust its cache so changes show up at once.
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['storefront'] });
    },
  });
}

      queryClient.setQueryData(CURRENT_USER_KEY, user);
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: CURRENT_USER_KEY });
    },
  });
}

    },
  });

/**
 * Permanently delete the account. Clears every trace of the session locally
 * and navigates home â€” the data itself is cascade-deleted server-side.
 */
export function useDeleteAccount() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  return useMutation<void, ApiError, DeleteAccountRequest>({
    mutationFn: (data) => usersApi.deleteAccount(data),
    onSuccess: () => {

    onError: () => {
      // A failed deletion attempt must never leave a half-cleared session,
      // but if the server says unauthorized the local session is stale.
    },

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\lib\buyerProfile.ts =====

/**
 * Buyer-specific profile extras (level / department / school).
 *
 * The API contract (docs/API_CONTRACT.md -> Users) exposes only fullName,
 * phone and avatarUrl on PATCH /users/me â€” academic details are not part of
 * it. They are therefore persisted client-side so the Buyer Profile form
 * keeps its values across reloads in BOTH mock and real API modes, while the
 * fields that ARE in the contract (full name) go through usersApi.
 */

const BUYER_PROFILE_KEY = 'universe.buyerProfile.v1';

export interface BuyerProfileExtras {
  level: string;
  department: string;
  school: string;
}

const EMPTY_EXTRAS: BuyerProfileExtras = { level: '', department: '', school: '' };

/** Read the persisted buyer extras; corrupted values fall back to blanks. */
export function loadBuyerExtras(): BuyerProfileExtras {
  try {
    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(BUYER_PROFILE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return { ...EMPTY_EXTRAS };
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    return {
      level: typeof parsed?.level === 'string' ? parsed.level : '',
      department: typeof parsed?.department === 'string' ? parsed.department : '',
      school: typeof parsed?.school === 'string' ? parsed.school : '',
    };
  } catch {
    return { ...EMPTY_EXTRAS };
  }
}

/** Best-effort write; private mode or full quota must never break the UI. */
export function saveBuyerExtras(extras: BuyerProfileExtras): void {
  try {
    window.localStorage.setItem(BUYER_PROFILE_KEY, JSON.stringify(extras));
  } catch {
    /* storage unavailable â€” in-memory state still works for this session */
  }
}

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\lib\googleIdentity.ts =====

/**
 * Google Identity Services (GIS) integration â€” the REAL Google sign-in flow.
 *
 * "Continue with Google" renders Google's OFFICIAL button (localized label
 * "Continue with Google"). Clicking it opens Google's own account chooser and
 * hands back a signed ID token (JWT), which is forwarded opaquely to
 * authApi.googleLogin() (POST /auth/google). The real backend verifies the
 * token server-side â€” the frontend never touches Google secrets.
 *
 * One-time setup (no extra dependencies):
 * 1. Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> Create
 *    credentials -> OAuth client ID -> Web application.
 * 2. Add every origin the app runs on (e.g. http://localhost:5173 and your
 *    dev-tunnel URL) to "Authorized JavaScript origins".
 * 3. Put the client ID in .env as VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and restart the dev
 *    server (see .env.example).
 */
import { apiConfig } from '../api/config';

/** Shown when the Google OAuth client id is missing from the environment. */
export const GOOGLE_SETUP_MESSAGE =
  'Google sign-in is not configured yet. Create an OAuth client ID (Web application) in Google Cloud Console, add this site to its authorized origins, and set VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in your .env file (see .env.example), then restart the dev server.';

/** Credential response handed back by GIS after the user picks an account. */
interface GoogleCredentialResponse {
  credential?: string;
}

/** Error-callback payload (moment failures: popup closed, origin mismatchâ€¦). */
interface GoogleIdError {
  type?: string;
  message?: string;
}

/** The small slice of the GIS API this app uses. */
export interface GoogleIdApi {
  initialize(config: {
    client_id: string;
    callback: (response: GoogleCredentialResponse) => void;
    error_callback?: (error: GoogleIdError) => void;
    auto_select?: boolean;
  }): void;
  renderButton(parent: HTMLElement, options: Record<string, unknown>): void;
  prompt(): void;
  disableAutoSelect(): void;
}

declare global {
  interface Window {
    google?: { accounts: { id: GoogleIdApi } };
  }
}

/** True when a Google OAuth client id is configured via VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. */
export function isGoogleConfigured(): boolean {
  return Boolean(apiConfig.googleClientId);
}

let loaderPromise: Promise<GoogleIdApi> | null = null;

/** Load https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client exactly once. */
export function loadGoogleIdentity(): Promise<GoogleIdApi> {
  if (window.google?.accounts?.id) return Promise.resolve(window.google.accounts.id);
  if (loaderPromise) return loaderPromise;

  loaderPromise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const timeout = window.setTimeout(() => {
      loaderPromise = null; // allow a retry on the next mount/click
      reject(new Error('Google sign-in took too long to load. Check your connection and try again.'));
    }, 15_000);

    const script = document.createElement('script');
    script.src = 'https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client';
    script.async = true;
    script.defer = true;
    script.onload = () => {
      window.clearTimeout(timeout);
      const api = window.google?.accounts?.id;
      if (api) {
        resolve(api);
      } else {
        loaderPromise = null;
        reject(new Error('Google sign-in loaded but is unavailable in this browser.'));
      }
    };
    script.onerror = () => {
      window.clearTimeout(timeout);
      loaderPromise = null; // allow a retry on the next mount/click
      reject(new Error('Could not load Google sign-in. Check your connection and try again.'));
    };
    document.head.appendChild(script);
  });

  return loaderPromise;
}

/** Human messages for the GIS error-callback types we care about. */
const ERROR_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  popup_closed_by_user: 'The Google sign-in window was closed before finishing.',
  popup_failed_to_open: 'Google could not open its sign-in window. Allow popups for this site and try again.',
  access_denied: 'Google sign-in was cancelled.',
  origin_mismatch: 'This siteâ€™s address is not listed as an authorized origin in the Google Cloud OAuth client.',
  client_id_missing: GOOGLE_SETUP_MESSAGE,
  client_id_not_valid: 'The configured VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is not a valid Google OAuth client ID.',
};

/**
 * Render Google's official sign-in button into `container` (replacing its
 * content). The button label is "Continue with Google" (localized by Google).
 * `onCredential` receives the signed Google ID token (JWT); `onError`
 * receives a human-readable message for any GIS moment failure.
 */
export async function renderGoogleButton(
  container: HTMLElement,
  onCredential: (credential: string) => void,
  onError?: (message: string) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  const googleId = await loadGoogleIdentity();

  // The container may have been unmounted while the script was loading
  // (e.g. the user navigated away) â€” never render into a detached node.
  if (!container.isConnected) return;

  // Re-rendering into the same container must replace, not stack, the button.
  // Also guards against React StrictMode's double effect run: once a Google
  // iframe has been rendered for this client id, skip (GIS replaces existing
  // buttons on re-initialize anyway, so this only prevents a wasted pass).
  if (container.dataset.googleRendered === apiConfig.googleClientId) return;

  container.innerHTML = '';

  googleId.initialize({
    client_id: apiConfig.googleClientId,
    // No One-Tap prompt on page load â€” the user explicitly clicked the button.
    auto_select: false,
    callback: (response) => {
      const credential = response?.credential;
      if (credential) onCredential(credential);
    },
    error_callback: (error) => {
      onError?.(error?.message || ERROR_MESSAGES[error?.type ?? ''] || 'Google sign-in failed. Please try again.');
    },
  });

  // GIS wants a numeric pixel width; clamp it to its supported range.
  const width = Math.min(400, Math.max(220, container.clientWidth || 350));
  googleId.renderButton(container, {
    type: 'standard',
    theme: 'outline',
    size: 'large',
    text: 'continue_with',
    shape: 'rectangular',
    logo_alignment: 'left',
    width,
  });
  // The iframe is now live for this client id.
  container.dataset.googleRendered = apiConfig.googleClientId;
}

/** Forget the Google-chosen account in this browser (used after sign-out). */
export function disableGoogleAutoSelect(): void {
  window.google?.accounts?.id.disableAutoSelect();
}

/** Size the stored product image aims for (~70KB), shared by card + detail. */

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\lib\image.js =====

/**
 * Client-side image processing for product uploads.
 *
 * The mock backend stores images as data URLs, so uploads are compressed in
 * the browser (downscale + JPEG re-encode) before being persisted â€” the same
 * technique real frontends use to cut upload sizes before hitting an API.
 */

const MAX_INPUT_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB source limit
const MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 500_000; // keep the compressed data URL reasonable

/**
 * Size the product-image pipeline aims for. The seller's photo is compressed
 * into ONE ~70KB WebP file, and that single file is used by BOTH the
 * marketplace card and the product detail view â€” no separate card/detail or
 * HD/zoom variants are produced, and the original file is discarded.
 */
export const PRODUCT_IMAGE_TARGET_BYTES = 70 * 1024;

/** Source limit mirrored by POST /uploads/images (the backend enforces its own). */
export const MAX_SOURCE_IMAGE_BYTES = MAX_INPUT_BYTES;

/** Longest-edge cap for the stored product image (card + detail share it). */
const PRODUCT_IMAGE_MAX_DIM = 1280;

function readAsDataUrl(file) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => resolve(String(reader.result));
    reader.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Could not read the selected file.'));
    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
  });
}

/**
 * Read a File as a data URL WITHOUT re-encoding it. Used by the mock upload
 * adapter for files that were already compressed by the product form.
 */
export function fileToDataUrl(file) {
  if (!file) throw new Error('No file selected.');
  return readAsDataUrl(file);
}

function loadImage(src) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const img = new Image();
    img.onload = () => resolve(img);
    img.onerror = () => reject(new Error('That file is not a valid image.'));
    img.src = src;
  });
}

function canvasToBlob(canvas, type, quality) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    canvas.toBlob(
      (blob) => (blob ? resolve(blob) : reject(new Error('Could not encode the image.'))),
      type,
      quality,
    );
  });
}

/**
 * Convert an image File to a compressed JPEG data URL, downscaled so its
 * longest edge is at most `maxDim` px.
 */
export async function fileToCompressedDataUrl(file, { maxDim = 900, quality = 0.75 } = {}) {
  if (!file) throw new Error('No file selected.');
  if (!file.type.startsWith('image/')) throw new Error('Only image files are allowed.');
  if (file.size > MAX_INPUT_BYTES) throw new Error('Image must be 5MB or smaller.');

  const sourceUrl = await readAsDataUrl(file);
  let image;
  try {
    image = await loadImage(sourceUrl);
  } catch {
    throw new Error('That file is not a valid image.');
  }

  const scale = Math.min(1, maxDim / Math.max(image.width || 1, image.height || 1));
  const width = Math.max(1, Math.round((image.width || maxDim) * scale));
  const height = Math.max(1, Math.round((image.height || maxDim) * scale));

  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = width;
  canvas.height = height;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  if (!ctx) throw new Error('Your browser does not support image processing.');
  ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, width, height);

  let dataUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', quality);
  // Second pass at a lower quality if the first is still too big.
  if (dataUrl.length > MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS) {
    dataUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.5);
  }
  if (dataUrl.length > MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS) {
    throw new Error('Image is still too large after compression â€” try a smaller file.');
  }
  return dataUrl;
}

/**
 * Compress one selected photo into a SINGLE ~70KB WebP file.
 *
 * Used by the product form at SUBMIT time (never while the seller is still
 * filling the form in). The same returned file backs BOTH the product card and
 * the product detail view â€” no separate card/detail or HD/zoom variants are
 * produced â€” and the original selection is discarded as soon as the compressed
 * file exists, so the seller's full-resolution photo is never uploaded.
 *
 * Quality is stepped down first, then the pixel dimensions, until the encoded
 * WebP fits `targetBytes`. Browsers that cannot encode WebP fall back to JPEG.
 *
 * @returns a File ready to POST to /uploads/images.
 */
export async function fileToProductImageFile(file, {
  targetBytes = PRODUCT_IMAGE_TARGET_BYTES,
  maxDim = PRODUCT_IMAGE_MAX_DIM,
} = {}) {
  if (!file) throw new Error('No image selected.');
  if (!file.type.startsWith('image/')) throw new Error('Only image files are allowed.');
  if (file.size > MAX_INPUT_BYTES) throw new Error('Image must be 5MB or smaller.');

  // Decode straight from an object URL and revoke it immediately after â€” the
  // original file is never re-read once we have the pixels.
  const objectUrl = URL.createObjectURL(file);
  let image;
  try {
    image = await loadImage(objectUrl);
  } catch {
    throw new Error('That file is not a valid image.');
  } finally {
    URL.revokeObjectURL(objectUrl);
  }

  const scale = Math.min(1, maxDim / Math.max(image.width || 1, image.height || 1));
  let width = Math.max(1, Math.round((image.width || maxDim) * scale));
  let height = Math.max(1, Math.round((image.height || maxDim) * scale));

  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = width;
  canvas.height = height;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  if (!ctx) throw new Error('Your browser does not support image processing.');
  ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, width, height);

  const qualities = [0.82, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.42];
  let mimeType = 'image/webp';
  let blob = await canvasToBlob(canvas, mimeType, qualities[0]);
  if (blob.type !== 'image/webp') {
    // The browser ignored the WebP request (it silently returns PNG then) â€”
    // JPEG is the next best single-file format.
    mimeType = 'image/jpeg';
    blob = await canvasToBlob(canvas, mimeType, qualities[0]);
  }

  for (const quality of qualities.slice(1)) {
    if (blob.size <= targetBytes) break;
    blob = await canvasToBlob(canvas, mimeType, quality);
  }

  // Quality alone was not enough â€” shrink the pixels and re-encode. The canvas
  // is cleared by resizing, so the source image is drawn again each round.
  let attempts = 0;
  while (blob.size > targetBytes && attempts < 4) {
    attempts += 1;
    const shrink = Math.max(0.55, Math.sqrt(targetBytes / blob.size));
    width = Math.max(1, Math.round(width * shrink));
    height = Math.max(1, Math.round(height * shrink));
    canvas.width = width;
    canvas.height = height;
    ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, width, height);
    blob = await canvasToBlob(canvas, mimeType, qualities[qualities.length - 1]);
  }

  const extension = mimeType === 'image/webp' ? 'webp' : 'jpg';
  return new File([blob], `product-image.${extension}`, {
    type: mimeType,
    lastModified: Date.now(),
  });
}

/**
 * Intent-based prefetching.
 *
 * The loaders below use EXACTLY the same import() specifiers as src/App.jsx,
 * so Rollup resolves them to the same modules â†’ the same output chunks.
 * Calling prefetch(key) warms the browser cache so a later route click
 * resolves near-instantly. Importing a module never executes component code â€”
 * it only fetches + parses the chunk in the background.
 */

const loaders = {
  home: () => import('../pages/HomePage'),
  auth: () => import('../components/auth/AuthPage'),
  seller: () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/SellerDashboard'),
  storefront: () => import('../components/storefront/StorefrontPage'),
  terms: () => import('../pages/TermsPage'),
  'dashboard/overview': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/DashboardOverview'),
  'dashboard/marketplace': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/MyMarketplace'),
  'dashboard/public-marketplace': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/PublicMarketplace'),
  'dashboard/sales': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/SalesAnalytics'),
  'dashboard/settings': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/SellerSettings'),
  'dashboard/profile': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/views/SellerProfile'),
  'dashboard/add-product': () => import('../components/seller-dashboard/ui/AddProductPage'),
};

const prefetched = new Set();

export const prefetch = (key) => {
  const load = loaders[key];
  if (!load || prefetched.has(key)) return;
  prefetched.add(key);
  // Ignore failures (offline etc.) so the Set doesn't block a retry later.
  load().catch(() => prefetched.delete(key));
};

/** Map a route path to the prefetch keys its navigation needs. */
const pathToKeys = {
  '/': ['home'],
  '/auth': ['auth'],
  '/auth/login': ['auth'],
  '/auth/signup': ['auth'],
  '/terms': ['terms'],
  '/marketplace': ['dashboard/public-marketplace'],
  '/seller': ['seller', 'dashboard/overview'],
  '/seller/marketplace': ['dashboard/marketplace'],
  '/seller/public-marketplace': ['dashboard/public-marketplace'],
  '/seller/sales': ['dashboard/sales'],
  '/seller/settings': ['dashboard/settings'],
  '/seller/profile': ['dashboard/profile'],
  '/seller/add-product': ['dashboard/add-product'],
};

/**
 * Signals the home page to begin loading its below-the-fold sections.
 * Used by in-page nav links (#marketplace, #dashboard, ...) so those sections
 * start loading the instant the user asks for them (before the scroll
 * observer would have kicked in).
 */
export const triggerHomeSectionsLoad = () => {
  try {
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event('universe:load-home-sections'));
  } catch (_) {
    /* no-op */
  }
};

/**
 * React event-handler factory: prefetch everything a Link needs the first time
 * the user hovers it or tab-focuses it, so the actual click is instant.
 * Attach via <Link {...prefetchPropsForPath('/seller')}>.
 */
export const prefetchPropsForPath = (path) => {
  const keys = pathToKeys[path] || [];
  const handle = () => keys.forEach(prefetch);
  return { onMouseEnter: handle, onFocus: handle };
};

/**
 * Store domain helpers â€” every registered seller automatically gets a
 * private-marketplace domain in the form `storename.<app-domain>`
 * (e.g. `globalstore.universe.market`).
 *
 * The slug is derived from the seller's store name, so naming a store
 * "Global Store" during onboarding instantly reserves the domain
 * globalstore.universe.market, which serves that seller's private storefront.
 *
 * Routing strategy:
 * - Production: `*.universe.market` is a wildcard-DNS + reverse-proxy setup
 *   that points any store subdomain at this SPA.
 * - Local dev: browsers already resolve `*.localhost` to 127.0.0.1, so
 *   `globalstore.localhost:5173` works out of the box with Vite.
 * - Everywhere else (ngrok tunnels, preview deploys â€” hosts where wildcard
 *   subdomains cannot be guaranteed): the canonical path alias
 *   `/store/:storeSlug` is used instead.
 */

/** Base domain of the app. Override with VITE_APP_DOMAIN in the environment. */
export const APP_DOMAIN = String(
  (import.meta.env && import.meta.env.VITE_APP_DOMAIN) || 'universe.market',
).replace(/^https?:\/\//, '');

/** Subdomain labels that must never resolve to a store. */
const RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = new Set(['www', 'app', 'api', 'admin', 'mail', 'ftp']);

/**
 * "Global Store!" -> "globalstore"
 * Lowercase, strip accents, drop anything that is not a letter or digit.
 * Returns '' when nothing usable remains.
 */
export function slugifyStoreName(name) {
  if (!name) return '';
  return String(name)
    .normalize('NFKD')
    .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '')
    .slice(0, 40);
}

/** Pretty display form: "globalstore.universe.market" (no protocol). */
export function getPrettyStoreDomain(slug) {
  return `${slug || 'store'}.${APP_DOMAIN}`;
}

/** Full URL form: "https://globalstore.universe.market". */
export function getStoreDomainUrl(slug) {
  return `https://${getPrettyStoreDomain(slug)}`;
}

/**
 * Parse a hostname and return the store slug when the host is a store domain:
 * `slug.localhost` (dev) or `slug.<APP_DOMAIN>` (production wildcard).
 * Returns null for the apex/unknown hosts so normal deployments keep using
 * the `/store/:storeSlug` path form.
 */
export function parseStoreSubdomain(hostname) {
  if (!hostname) return null;
  const host = String(hostname).toLowerCase().split(':')[0].replace(/\.$/, '');
  if (!host) return null;

  const isLocalStore = host.endsWith('.localhost');
  const isAppStore = Boolean(APP_DOMAIN) && host.endsWith(`.${APP_DOMAIN}`);
  if (!isLocalStore && !isAppStore) return null;

  const suffix = isLocalStore ? '.localhost' : `.${APP_DOMAIN}`;
  const slug = host.slice(0, host.length - suffix.length);
  if (!slug || slug.includes('.') || RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS.has(slug)) return null;
  return slug;
}

/**
 * Small user-related display helpers shared across the dashboard UI.
 */

/** "Ada Lovelace" -> "AL" (max 2 chars) for avatar chips. */
export function getUserInitials(name) {
  if (!name) return '?';
  const parts = name.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
  if (parts.length === 0) return '?';
  if (parts.length === 1) return parts[0].slice(0, 2).toUpperCase();
  return (parts[0][0] + parts[parts.length - 1][0]).toUpperCase();
}

/** "Ada Lovelace" -> "Ada" for greetings. */
export function getFirstName(name) {
  if (!name) return 'there';
  return name.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] || 'there';
}

/** Best-effort display name for a store: store name, else the user's name. */
export function getStoreDisplayName(storeName, fullName) {
  return (storeName && storeName.trim()) || (fullName && fullName.trim()) || 'My Store';
}

/** ISO timestamp -> "just now" / "5 mins ago" / "3 hours ago" / "2 days ago". */
export function timeAgo(iso) {
  const then = new Date(iso).getTime();
  if (Number.isNaN(then)) return '';
  const seconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor((Date.now() - then) / 1000));
  if (seconds < 60) return 'just now';
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
  if (minutes < 60) return `${minutes} min${minutes === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
  const hours = Math.floor(minutes / 60);
  if (hours < 24) return `${hours} hour${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
  const days = Math.floor(hours / 24);
  if (days < 30) return `${days} day${days === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
  const months = Math.floor(days / 30);
  return `${months} month${months === 1 ? '' : 's'} ago`;
}

/** "â‚¦1,249.50" style formatting for money values (Nigerian Naira). */
export function formatMoney(value) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
    style: 'currency',
    currency: 'NGN',
    maximumFractionDigits: 2,
  }).format(value);
}


===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\pages\HomePage.jsx =====

import { lazy, Suspense, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import Navbar from '../components/Navbar';
import HeroSection from '../components/HeroSection';

/**
 * Landing page composition with code splitting + progressive loading.
 *
 * Navbar + HeroSection (above the fold) are loaded eagerly so the first paint
 * is fast. Everything below the fold lives in ONE lazy chunk (HomeSections)
 * that is only fetched once the user scrolls near it (or clicks an in-page
 * anchor link). Nothing below the fold is downloaded on initial load.
 */
const HomeSections = lazy(() => import('./HomeSections'));

const HomePage = ({ cartCount, onAddToCart }) => {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const anchorRef = useRef(null);

  // Load below-the-fold content when the user scrolls near it.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined' || !anchorRef.current) {
      setReady(true);
      return;
    }
    const obs = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        if (entries.some((e) => e.isIntersecting)) {
          setReady(true);
          obs.disconnect();
        }
      },
      { rootMargin: '400px 0px' },
    );
    obs.observe(anchorRef.current);
    return () => obs.disconnect();
  }, []);

  // Also load immediately when an in-page nav link asks for it.
  useEffect(() => {
    const onRequest = () => setReady(true);
    window.addEventListener('universe:load-home-sections', onRequest);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('universe:load-home-sections', onRequest);
  }, []);

  return (
    <>
      <Navbar cartCount={cartCount} />
      <HeroSection />

      <div ref={anchorRef} className="home-sections-anchor" aria-hidden="true" />

      {ready ? (
        <Suspense fallback={<div className="section-loader" aria-hidden="true" />}>
          <HomeSections onAddToCart={onAddToCart} />
        </Suspense>
      ) : (
        <div className="home-sections-placeholder" aria-hidden="true" />
      )}
    </>
  );
};

export default HomePage;

===== C:\Users\Admin\Universe-frontend\Universe-frontend\universe-react\src\pages\HomeSections.jsx =====

import { lazy, Suspense, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

const FeaturesShowcase = lazy(() => import('../components/FeaturesShowcase'));
const DashboardSection = lazy(() => import('../components/DashboardSection'));
const ProductSection = lazy(() => import('../components/ProductSection'));
const ConnectionSection = lazy(() => import('../components/ConnectionSection'));
const Features = lazy(() => import('../components/Features'));
const CTA = lazy(() => import('../components/CTA'));
const Footer = lazy(() => import('../components/Footer'));

function Section({ children }) {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const sectionRef = useRef(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined' || !sectionRef.current) {
      setReady(true);
      return;
    }

    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      ([entry]) => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting) {
          setReady(true);
          observer.disconnect();
        }
      },
      { rootMargin: '600px 0px' },
    );
    observer.observe(sectionRef.current);
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div ref={sectionRef}>
      {ready ? (
        <Suspense fallback={<div className="section-loader" aria-hidden="true" />}>
          {children}
        </Suspense>
      ) : (
        <div className="section-loader" aria-hidden="true" />
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/**
 * Each section gets its own chunk and starts loading only as it approaches
 * the viewport. This keeps untouched lower-page content out of startup.
 */
const HomeSections = ({ onAddToCart }) => (
  <>
    <Section><FeaturesShowcase /></Section>
    <Section><DashboardSection /></Section>
    <Section><ProductSection onAddToCart={onAddToCart} /></Section>
    <Section><ConnectionSection /></Section>
    <Section><Features /></Section>
    <Section><CTA /></Section>
    <Section><Footer /></Section>
  </>
);

export default HomeSections;

    section.label,
    ...(section.paras ?? []),
    ...(section.list ?? []),
    ...(section.trail ?? []),
    ...(section.strong ?? []),
  ]
    .join(' ')
    .toLowerCase(),
}));
/** Clause card renderer â€” badge tone follows the original document. */
function renderSection(section) {
  const toneClass = section.tone === 'rose'
    ? ' tou-card-num--rose'
    : section.tone === 'slate'
      ? ' tou-card-num--slate'
      : '';

  return (
    <article key={section.id} className="tou-card" id={section.id} data-legal-section>
      <div className="tou-card-row">
        <span className={`tou-card-num${toneClass}`}>{section.num}</span>
        <div className="tou-card-body">
          <h2 className="tou-card-title">{section.title}</h2>
          {section.paras?.map((p, i) => (
            <p key={i} className="tou-card-p">{p}</p>
          ))}
          {section.label && <p className="tou-card-label">{section.label}</p>}
          {section.list && (
            <ul className={section.ordered ? 'tou-list tou-list--ordered' : 'tou-list'}>
              {section.list.map((item, i) => (
                <li key={i}>{item}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          )}
          {section.trail?.map((text, i) => (
            <p key={i} className="tou-card-trail">{text}</p>
          ))}
          {section.strong?.map((text, i) => (
            <p key={i} className="tou-card-trail--strong">{text}</p>
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>
    </article>
  );
}

function TermsPage() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
  const [agreed, setAgreed] = useState(false);
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false);
  const location = useLocation();

  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = 'UNIVERSE Terms of Service';
    return () => {
      document.title = 'Universe - Launch, Manage, and Scale Your Online Marketplace';
    };
  }, []);

  // Deep-link support: arriving from another page at /terms#section-N (e.g. the
  // home footer's "Sellers Agreement" â†’ /terms#section-3) scrolls that clause
  // card into view once it has rendered. The browser's native hash scroll runs
  // before React renders anything, so it never lands â€” this retries until the
  // target card exists. `.tou-card` already sets scroll-margin-top for the
  // sticky header.
  useEffect(() => {
    const hash = location.hash.replace(/^#/, '');
    if (!hash) return undefined;
    let cancelled = false;
    const tryScroll = (attempt) => {
      if (cancelled) return;
      const el = document.getElementById(hash);
      if (el) {
        el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });
        return;
      }
      if (attempt < 25) window.setTimeout(() => tryScroll(attempt + 1), 120);
    };
    const timer = window.setTimeout(() => tryScroll(0), 80);
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      window.clearTimeout(timer);
    };
  }, [location.pathname, location.hash]);

  // Live clause search â€” replicates the mockup's whatever-user-types filter.
  const visible = useMemo(() => {
    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (!q) return LEGAL_SECTIONS;
    return LEGAL_SECTIONS.filter((section) => section.searchText.includes(q));
  }, [query]);

  // Scroll-spy: highlight the TOC entry of whichever section is in view.
  useEffect(() => {
    const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.tou-toc-item'));
    const articles = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('article[data-legal-section]'));
    if (typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined' || articles.length === 0) return;
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {
        entries.forEach((entry) => {
          if (entry.isIntersecting) {
            const id = entry.target.getAttribute('id');
            links.forEach((link) => {
              if (link.getAttribute('href') === `#${id}`) link.classList.add('active');
              else link.classList.remove('active');
            });
          }
        });
      },
      { rootMargin: '-20% 0px -70% 0px' },
    );
    articles.forEach((article) => observer.observe(article));
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, [visible]);

  const handleAccept = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (agreed) setSubmitted(true);
  };

  return (
    <div className="tou-page" id="tou-top">
      {/* ---- Top navigation ---- */}
      <header className="tou-header">
        <div className="tou-header-inner">
          <Link to="/" className="tou-brand" aria-label="UNIVERSE Home">
            <img src="/logo.png" alt="Universe" className="tou-brand-logo" />
          </Link>

          <div className="tou-search-wrap">
            <div className="tou-search">
              <SearchIcon />
              <input
                className="tou-search-input"
                id="clause-search"
                type="text"
                placeholder="Search terms, seller rules, escrow..."
                value={query}
                onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
              />
            </div>
          </div>

          <div className="tou-actions">
            <button
              type="button"
              className="tou-btn-print tou-no-print"
              onClick={() => window.print()}
              title="Print or save as PDF"
            >
              <PrintIcon />
              <span className="tou-print-label">Print / Save PDF</span>
            </button>
            <a className="tou-btn-accept tou-no-print" href="#agreement-confirmation">
              Accept Terms
            </a>
          </div>
        </div>
      </header>

      {/* ---- Hero banner ---- */}
      <div className="tou-hero">
        <div className="tou-hero-glow" aria-hidden="true" />
        <div className="tou-hero-inner">
          <nav className="tou-breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
            <Link to="/">Home</Link>
            <ChevronIcon />
            <a href="#legal-center">Legal Center</a>
            <ChevronIcon />
            <span className="tou-breadcrumb-current">Terms of Service</span>
          </nav>

          <div className="tou-heading-wrap">
            <span className="tou-badge">
              <span className="tou-pulse" />
              Official Platform Governance â€¢ September 2026
            </span>
            <h1 className="tou-title">UNIVERSE TERMS OF SERVICE</h1>
            <p className="tou-preamble">
              These Terms of Service govern your access to and use of the UNIVERSE website,
              applications, software, online-store services, payment-related feature and other
              services provided by UNIVERSE.
            </p>
            <div className="tou-binding" role="note">
              <WarningIcon />
              <div>
                <strong>Binding Agreement:</strong> By creating an account with UNIVERSE, you
                agree to these Terms. If you do not agree to these Terms, you must not use the
                service.
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
{/* ---- Main content ---- */}
      <main className="tou-main">
        <div className="tou-grid">
          {/* Sticky sidebar: sections directory + help desk */}
          <aside className="tou-aside tou-no-print" aria-label="Table of contents">
            <div className="tou-toc-card">
              <div className="tou-toc-head">
